<<<FILE rules/writing-rules.md>>>

# Writing rules

These apply to every word of RoomIQ output: web, decks, scripts, release notes, in-app copy, and AI-generated text inside the product.
last_reviewed: 2026-11-13

## Mechanics
- No em dashes anywhere. Use commas, colons, or two sentences. En dashes stay only inside official metro names ("Dallas–Fort Worth").
- Banned words: leverage, unlock, seamless, robust, streamline, cutting-edge, empower, elevate, revolutionize, game-changing, best-in-class, world-class, supercharge, turbocharge, harness, delve, tapestry, testament, foster, facilitate, utilize, myriad, plethora, pivotal, crucial, vital, skyrocket, effortless, unparalleled, groundbreaking.
- "Leverage" is banned in its finance sense too. Say financing, debt, or loan-to-value.
- Avoid in their figurative sense: landscape, navigate, journey, realm.
- Paragraphs of one to three sentences. Front-load the point.
- Numbers over adjectives. Every number carries its unit and window: "$260 avg weekly asking, last 90 days", never "$260".
- Rents are weekly per room. Revenue is monthly per property. Say which.
- Use the product's own labels, spelled as the UI spells them (`rules/glossary.md`).

## Tone
Plain, numerate, and candid, like a good underwriting memo. The readers put their own money and debt behind a decision, so they trust evidence and distrust hype. When the evidence is thin, say so before they find out: RoomIQ's own UI does this ("Fallback support", "Confidence Low"), and the copy matches it.

Right register: an analyst explaining a comp set. Wrong register: "passive income" real estate marketing, urgency tricks, and lifestyle promises.

## Writing for the ear (demos, video, webinars)
- Short spoken sentences. One clause where you would write two.
- Second person, one listener, contractions.
- Say what is on screen before you interpret it: "This tile shows 87.5 percent occupancy."
- Say confidence labels out loud. Never skip "fallback" or "low confidence" for pacing.
- Read it aloud before it ships. Cut what you stumble on.

## Claim discipline
Check every "only", "first", "best", "never", "most", and "fastest" against `rules/do-not-say.md`. Check every capability against `rules/feature-status.md`: UNVERIFIED capabilities are named, never described. A conditional claim names its condition in the same sentence ("in covered markets", "on RoomIQ Pro", "when local evidence is thin"). Every financial output carries "for information, not financial advice" on the same surface.

## Channel discipline
Working channel mix (G01, pending founder confirmation):
- In: founder-led demos and sales calls, data-led education content, community participation, product-led trial, product and release copy.
- Not yet: paid ads and cold outreach at volume. If asked, say it is out of scope for this go-to-market today and offer the nearest in-scope channel (a community post, a warm follow-up, a content piece).
- Never: publishing market statistics as a dataset or report until data rights are confirmed (G11, G12).

## Signature lines (checked, founder approval pending)
- "Underwrite the room, not just the house."
- "Every number shows its evidence."
- "When the evidence is thin, RoomIQ says so."
- "The math is on the screen."

## Formatting
Prose first. Lists only for real lists. Headlines short and concrete. Sentence case for headings. No emoji in RoomIQ copy, even though listing titles carry them.

## Before returning any draft
Run `ops/QA-checklist.md`, then name in one line the rule the draft came closest to breaking.

<<<END rules/writing-rules.md>>>


<<<FILE rules/do-not-say.md>>>

# Do not say

The claim hygiene spine. Left column is forbidden or risky; right column is the safe replacement. Quoted phrases on the left are matched by `tools/brain.py lint`.
last_reviewed: 2026-11-13

## Hard bans

| Do not say | Say instead |
|---|---|
| Accuracy: "accurate forecast", "precise", "predicts revenue", "within X%", "proven model" | "Every forecast shows its formula, its comps, and a confidence label." No backtest exists (G14). |
| Universal coverage: "any market", "every property", "complete coverage", "all US markets" | "Underwrite any US address. Where nearby evidence is thin, RoomIQ labels the forecast fallback support and shows its confidence." |
| Coverage numbers: "properties tracked", "rooms tracked", "thousands of listings" | Nothing until G13 is answered. Screenshot counts (412 in DFW) are one capture, not a claim. |
| Data source: "PadSplit data", "scraped", "official data", "partnered with", "integrated with" | "Built from observed room listings in the markets RoomIQ covers." Never name or imply a source or partner (G11). |
| Real time: "real-time", "live data" | "Metrics show their as-of date." |
| Income language: "income", "earnings", "collected rent", "cash flow guaranteed" | "Estimated rental revenue, based on observed rents and occupancy, not collected payments." |
| Financial advice: "best deals", "guaranteed returns", "will cash flow", "bank-approved", "lender-ready" | "Model cash flow, cash-on-cash, DSCR, and cap rate from the forecast and your own inputs. For information, not financial advice." |
| Legal status: "legal in your city", "compliant", "zoning approved", "local law" | "Compare an operating checklist with recorded local policies. Not legal advice; confirm local rules." |
| AI everywhere: "AI-powered", "AI predicts", "machine learning forecast" | Name the capability. Only visual comps and AI concepts carry AI framing (G19). |
| AI concepts as results: "after photo", "your renovated room", "see the results", "boost rent by" | "Preview an AI concept of an upgrade, watermarked as AI-generated. No validated economics yet." |
| Visual comps as value: "worth the same", "value comps", "equally valuable" | "Rooms that look like this one, with their weekly price and days to fill." |
| Market Score internals: "Market Score measures", "based on demand and supply" | "A 0 to 100 Market Score with a letter grade." (G18) |
| Prices and limits: "pricing starts at", "plan costs", "free trial", "unlimited plan", "money-back" | Nothing. Pricing is undecided (G07). `RoomIQ Pro` may be named as shown. |
| Invented proof: testimonials, customer counts, "investors trust", "users earn" | The closed proof set in `ops/copy-bank.md`. Customer proof today: none. Write `[PROOF POINT NEEDED]`. |
| Unverified features described: what amenity ROI, house rules, rent guidance, layouts, cohorts, or forecasts return | Name them as present in the product. Describe output only after status moves to SHIPPED. |
| Flood: "flood risk score", "insurance determination" | "Check the FEMA flood hazard layer on the map. Not an insurance or regulatory determination." |
| Category confusion: "Airbnb", "short-term rental", "vacation rental" | "rent-by-the-room", "weekly room rents". |

## Fair housing, never negotiable
House rules, ads, and resident criteria never reference race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, disability, or any class a state adds (often source of income). Do not say "women only", "no kids", "Christian home", "no vouchers". Say instead: rules about conduct and use of the property, applied to every resident.

## In demos, video, and screenshots
- Demo only in well-covered metros (Dallas, Austin, Houston, Atlanta, Phoenix, Tampa). Never an uncovered address (D-Q28).
- Never show the Q26 banner, the Deal Calculator defaults, or a closet visual comp as a talking point.
- AI concepts appear with the watermark visible. Never crop it.
- Public screenshots blur host names and listing photos until G12 is answered.
- Verbatim product disclaimers stay verbatim: "Based on observed rents and occupancy, not collected payments." and "AI-generated concept for visualization only — this image does not depict the actual current condition of the property."

## Claims that need scoping (verify before print)
- **"The only room-level analytics tool."** Counter-example: platform-native host tools show room price against the metro average and a market map; SFR Analytics published room-for-rent aggregates. Safe form: "Analytics built at the room level: weekly room price, room occupancy, fill speed, and bath and size segments."
- **"First AI underwriting for coliving."** Unverifiable. Hard ban.
- **"Better than AirDNA."** Counter-example: AirDNA has deeper short-term rental history. Safe form: "AirDNA is built for nightly stays. RoomIQ models weekly room rents and room occupancy."
- **"Transparent forecasts."** Holds. The formula, support level, comp distance, and confidence are on the results screen (screen 14).
- **"Underwrite any US address."** Holds only with the fallback clause attached in the same sentence.

## Historical and reputational material
None known (G08). Do not repeat rumors about any marketplace or competitor. Platform-specific claims about rivals come only from `reference/competitor-battlecards.md`, dated.

<<<END rules/do-not-say.md>>>


<<<FILE rules/feature-status.md>>>

# Feature status ledger

Governs what can be promised. Update this file the moment status changes, before any copy follows.
last_reviewed: 2026-11-13

Legend, graded by evidence because the only source so far is 15 product screenshots (2026-11-10):
- **SHIPPED**: seen working in the product. Present tense, described only as far as the screens show.
- **PARTIAL**: partly seen. Describe the visible part only.
- **UNVERIFIED**: the control exists in the UI, the output was never captured. Name it, never describe what it returns. Founder confirms (G03).
- **IN BUILD**: committed, not shipped. "Coming soon" or omit. None confirmed today.
- **ROADMAP**: inferred direction. Never a launch claim.

Line format, parsed by `tools/brain.py`: `- **ID Name** [aliases]: STATUS. Note.`

## Discover (Dashboard)
- **C01 Market search and selection** [market picker, choose markets]: SHIPPED. City, ZIP, or metro group, up to 3 per dashboard.
- **C02 Market ranking by Market Score** [top us markets, leaderboard, market score]: PARTIAL. Ranked list seen; score inputs unknown.
- **C03 Seasonality analysis** [seasonality, fill speed curve]: SHIPPED. Occupancy and fill speed, with a national fallback label.
- **C04 Market forecasts** [forecasts tab, market forecast]: UNVERIFIED.
- **C05 Submarket demand map** [hex cells, occupancy health, submarket signals]: SHIPPED. Evidence-adjusted cells, Strong, Watch, Weak, Thin.
- **C06 Supply map with listing status** [explore map, listing status]: SHIPPED. Listed, Coming soon, Never listed, Delisted.
- **C07 Flood-risk overlay** [fema, flood]: UNVERIFIED. Toggle seen, layer never rendered.
- **C08 Market filters** [advanced filters, dormant properties]: UNVERIFIED.
- **C09 Saved views** [saved view]: UNVERIFIED.
- **C10 Market report export** [market report]: UNVERIFIED. Button looked disabled in the capture.

## Analyze (Property Analyzer)
- **C11 Property search** [search by city, property id]: SHIPPED. Matches listing-title text as well as city.
- **C12 Property performance and revenue** [performance snapshot, estimated rental revenue]: SHIPPED.
- **C13 Property signal and recommendation** [property signal, useful benchmark]: SHIPPED. One label seen; full label set unknown.
- **C14 Room-segment economics** [room segments, bathroom premium, best spread]: SHIPPED.
- **C15 Rolling performance windows** [rolling windows, 7d, 30d, 90d]: SHIPPED.
- **C16 Evidence quality scoring** [evidence quality, completeness]: PARTIAL.
- **C17 Visual comps** [visually similar rooms, similar rooms]: SHIPPED. Searches across markets, not only the local one.
- **C18 AI upgrade concepts** [media studio, ai concept]: SHIPPED. Five presets seen; output watermarked.
- **C19 Property trends** [trends tab]: UNVERIFIED.
- **C20 Room-level history** [rooms tab, room history]: UNVERIFIED.

## Underwrite (Property Predictor)
- **C21 Nearby supply check** [nearby coliving supply]: SHIPPED. About 3 miles around any US address.
- **C22 Bedroom layout recommendation** [compare layouts, bedroom mix]: UNVERIFIED.
- **C23 Amenity ROI shortlist** [amenity roi, recommend amenities]: UNVERIFIED.
- **C24 House rules checklist** [house rules, recommend rules]: UNVERIFIED.
- **C25 Per-room rent guidance** [rent guidance, price optimizer]: UNVERIFIED.
- **C26 Cohort lease-up outcomes** [cohort outcomes, lease-up]: UNVERIFIED.
- **C27 Revenue forecast for any address** [forecast, decision board, stabilized revenue]: SHIPPED. Formula, support, and confidence shown. See defect D-Q26.
- **C28 Forecast stability test** [evidence lookback]: SHIPPED.
- **C29 Comp set review** [support details, caution flags]: UNVERIFIED.
- **C30 Garage conversion scenario** [garage conversion]: UNVERIFIED.

## Decide and Monitor
- **C31 Deal calculator** [deal calculator, cash on cash, dscr, cap rate]: PARTIAL. Inputs seen, outputs never captured. Pro only.
- **C32 Saved underwrites with re-run** [my underwrites, saved underwrites]: PARTIAL. Empty state only.

## Roadmap, inferred and never claimable
- **R01 Upgrade economics per AI concept** [upgrade economics]: ROADMAP. From "no validated economics for this edit yet".
- **R02 Alerts on market moves** [market alerts, market-move alerts]: ROADMAP. Not seen anywhere; implied by the re-run copy.
- **R03 Markets outside the US** [international markets, outside the us]: ROADMAP. Only hint is "this country's" in one helper line.

## Known defects that gate claims
- D-Q26: forecast banner says full bedroom count, the math uses 1.0 active rooms.
- D-Q28: uncovered addresses still forecast, on comps a median 82.88 mi away.
- D-Q30: Deal Calculator interest default may read 22%. D-Q31: vacancy may double count.
- D-Q18: closet photos appear as visual comps.

## Demo rule
Nothing UNVERIFIED, IN BUILD, or ROADMAP is screen-recorded, narrated, or shown as if a customer can do it today. No demo crosses a known defect. See `reference/demo-playbook.md`.

<<<FILE rules/glossary.md>>>

# Glossary, canonical vocabulary

Mirrors the product UI exactly. Where the UI and a draft disagree, the UI wins. Terms marked (confirm) carry a working definition pending founder sign-off (`ops/founder-gap-interview.md`).
last_reviewed: 2026-11-13

## Brand and modules

| Term | Rule |
|---|---|
| RoomIQ | One word, capital R, I, Q. Never "Room IQ", "Roomiq", or "ROOMIQ" in prose. The wordmark is spaced caps; prose is not. |
| RoomIQ Pro | The only plan name visible in the product. Name it only as shown. No other tier names. |
| Dashboard | Market-level view: market picker, Overview, Trends, Forecasts tabs, Explore map. Capitalized. |
| Property Analyzer | Property-level deep dive. "the Analyzer" on second mention. Never "analyser". |
| Property Predictor | Underwriting flow for any US address. "the Predictor" on second mention. |
| Deal Calculator | Step 5 of the Predictor, marked Pro in the product. |
| My Underwrites | Saved property or market reports that can be re-run. |
| Media Studio | AI concept images of upgrades on listing photos. |
| Visually Similar Rooms | Image-similarity comps. Short form: "visual comps". |
| Explore map | The Dashboard map with submarket cells and property dots. |

## Metrics and outputs

| Term | Rule |
|---|---|
| Market Score | A 0 to 100 score with a letter grade. Never describe its inputs (confirm). |
| Occupancy | Occupied rooms divided by total rooms. Room-level, never unit-level. |
| Avg weekly asking | Mean asking rent per room per week. Rents are weekly in this category. |
| Fill speed, days to fill | How fast a vacant room is re-leased (confirm formula). |
| Occupancy Health | Submarket cell signal from observed occupied rooms. |
| Strong, Watch, Weak, Thin | Occupancy Score bands. "Thin" means too little evidence, never "low demand". |
| Evidence Quality | Completeness, history coverage, and media count for one property. |
| Property Signal | The action label on a property (seen: `Useful benchmark`) plus its recommendation. |
| Best spread | Largest average weekly price gap between room segments. |
| Room segment | Rooms grouped by bathroom (Private, Shared) or size (Cozy, Standard). |
| Rolling windows | 7, 30, and 90-day views of occupancy, daily price, volatility, and deltas. |
| Estimated rental revenue | Observed asking rents times occupancy for a window. Never "income", "earnings", or "collected". |
| Forecast | The Predictor's monthly revenue output. Use "forecast" for the output and "baseline profile" for the inputs. Never "baseline" for the output. |
| Fallback support | Local evidence was thin, so broader comps were used. Always shown with the confidence label. |
| Confidence | The forecast's label (seen: Low). Never translate into a percentage. |
| Illustrative scenarios | Plus and minus 10 percent of the forecast. Never "range", "interval", or "bounds". |
| Model routing | Automatic choice between the tracked-history path and the bounded underwriting path. |
| Evidence lookback | The window of market evidence (default 270 days) behind priors and comps. |
| Underwrite | Noun: a saved report in My Underwrites. Verb: to run a property through the Predictor. |
| AI concept | A watermarked, AI-generated edit of a listing photo. Never "render", "preview of results", or "after photo". |

## Category words

| Term | Rule |
|---|---|
| rent-by-the-room | The category, hyphenated as an adjective. Investors search for this phrase. |
| coliving | One word, lowercase, as in the product ("Nearby coliving supply"). Not "co-living" in RoomIQ copy. |
| residents | The people who rent rooms. Not "members" (a marketplace's own term), not "boarders". Avoid "tenants": legal status varies by state. |
| investors, operators | The two audiences. Never blend them in one asset. See `reference/icp-personas.md`. |
| short-term rental, Airbnb | Banned as descriptions of RoomIQ or its category. RoomIQ models weekly room rents, not nightly stays. |
| AI-powered | Banned as a blanket label. Name the capability: visual comps, AI concepts. |

## The distinction that must never blur

**Estimated** versus **actual**. Every RoomIQ number is an estimate built from observed listings, and it travels with its evidence: the as-of date, the support level, the confidence label. A forecast is never "accurate", an estimate is never "income", and an AI concept is never the property.

<<<END rules/glossary.md>>>


<<<FILE ops/QA-checklist.md>>>

# QA checklist, run before shipping any output

Every item is answerable yes or no by looking at the draft. Run the mechanical part first: `python3 tools/brain.py lint <draft.md>` catches em dashes, banned words, superlatives, ledger phrases, and mentions of non-shipped capabilities. Then tick the rest by reading.

## Writing
- [ ] No em dashes anywhere.
- [ ] None of the banned words in `rules/writing-rules.md`, including "leverage" in its finance sense.
- [ ] Paragraphs of one to three sentences, point first.
- [ ] Every number carries its unit and window (per room per week, per property per month, last 90 days).
- [ ] No emoji.

## Channel
- [ ] The asset is for an in-scope channel in `rules/writing-rules.md`. Paid ads or cold outreach at volume: stop and redirect.
- [ ] No market statistics published as a dataset or report (data rights open, G11 and G12).

## Claims
- [ ] No accuracy language about forecasts. Transparency language only.
- [ ] "Any US address" always carries the fallback clause in the same sentence.
- [ ] No coverage numbers, no named data source, no partner or affiliation claim.
- [ ] Every capability mentioned is checked in `rules/feature-status.md`. UNVERIFIED ones are named, never described. ROADMAP ones are absent.
- [ ] No price, trial, limit, or tier name other than `RoomIQ Pro`.
- [ ] No proof point outside the closed set in `ops/copy-bank.md`. Gaps marked `[PROOF POINT NEEDED]`.
- [ ] Revenue is "estimated rental revenue", never income or earnings.
- [ ] Every financial output carries "for information, not financial advice" on the same surface.
- [ ] House rules and resident criteria reference no protected class.
- [ ] Every "only", "first", "best", "never", "most", "fastest" checked against `rules/do-not-say.md`.

## Naming and strategy
- [ ] Module and metric names match `rules/glossary.md` exactly ("Property Predictor", "Evidence Quality", "coliving").
- [ ] "Forecast" names the output; "baseline profile" names the inputs.
- [ ] No framing that contradicts `ops/decisions.md`, including WORKING decisions.

## Audience and stage
- [ ] One audience only: investors or operators. Not both.
- [ ] Copy matches one funnel stage in `reference/customer-journey.md`.

## Demos, video, screenshots
- [ ] Demo address is in a well-covered metro, never an uncovered one.
- [ ] No known defect on screen (D-Q26 banner, Deal Calculator defaults, closet visual comps).
- [ ] AI concepts shown with the watermark visible.
- [ ] Host names and listing photos blurred in anything public.
- [ ] Confidence and support labels read out loud, not skipped.
- [ ] Nothing UNVERIFIED is shown as if a customer can do it today.

## Voice
- [ ] Reads like the matching file in `examples/`.
- [ ] One line at the end names the rule the draft came closest to breaking.

## After shipping
- [ ] Asset filed in `pages/` or listed in `ops/asset-index.md`.
- [ ] An entry in `ops/activity-log.md` with the experiment or assumption it tests.
- [ ] Anything the work taught you logged in `ops/signal-log.md`.

<<<END ops/QA-checklist.md>>>


<<<FILE reference/product-surface.md>>>

# Product surface, RoomIQ as built

Load for: describing what RoomIQ does, writing walkthroughs, release notes, demo scripts, or support answers. Distills: S1 screen inventory and S2 working notes (IA, entities).

Everything here is FACT from the 2026-11-10 captures unless marked. Status per capability lives in `rules/feature-status.md`; this file describes shape, not status.

## Information architecture

```
RoomIQ
  ANALYTICS
    Dashboard            gate: choose up to 3 cities, ZIPs, or a metro group
      Overview (n props) Top US markets by Market Score
      Trends             Seasonality: Occupancy | Fill speed, national fallback
      Forecasts          (never opened)
      Explore map        clusters, hex submarket cells, layers, FEMA toggle
      Property drawer    KPIs, estimated revenue, hand-offs to Predictor and Analyzer
    Property Analyzer    Search -> Pick property -> Analyze
      Overview           Property Signal, Performance Snapshot, segments,
                         rolling windows, Evidence Quality, Visually Similar
                         Rooms, Media Studio, Property Photos
      Trends, Rooms      (never opened)
  PREDICTOR
    Property Predictor   Location -> Baseline -> Forecast -> Results
      1 Location         address or pin, nearby coliving supply (~3 mi)
      2 Baseline Profile core specs, bathroom mix, amenity ROI, house rules,
                         room pricing, cohort outcomes, room mix, access
      3 Run Forecast     model routing (Automatic), evidence lookback (270d)
      4 Decision Board   monthly revenue, support, confidence, scenarios,
                         best next step, garage conversion
      5 Deal Calculator  Pro: scenario, income, purchase, financing
      My Underwrites     saved reports, re-run against the market
  Global                 RoomIQ Pro badge, theme toggle, Privacy choices
```

## The workflow the product is built around

Discover a market (Dashboard), inspect comparable properties (Analyzer), underwrite a target (Predictor), model financed returns (Deal Calculator), save and monitor (My Underwrites). The drawer button "Forecast Stabilized Revenue" connects the Dashboard to the Predictor.

## Data entities visible in the product

| Entity | Fields seen |
|---|---|
| Market | name, type (city, ZIP, metro), property count, Market Score, grade, badge, occupancy, trend per month |
| Submarket cell | Occupancy Health, band (Strong, Watch, Weak, Thin), snapshot date |
| Property | title, host display name, city, type, bedrooms, bathrooms, rooms total, occupied, available, occupancy, avg weekly asking, move-in fee, reviews, price drops, status, signal, evidence level |
| Room segment | dimension (bath, size), value, room count, avg weekly, 90-day occupancy |
| Rolling window | 7, 30, 90 days: occupancy, avg daily price, volatility, occupancy delta, price delta |
| Similar-room match | match percent, price per week, days to fill, location |
| Baseline profile | type, bedrooms, bathrooms, square feet, private-bath rooms, room entries, common space, garage, transit distance |
| Forecast result | monthly revenue, formula terms, model path, lookback, support, confidence, comp count, median comp distance, scenarios, next step |
| Deal scenario | scenario, revenue, other income, vacancy, price, ARV, concessions, closing costs, financing mode, down payment, rate |

## Numbers that reconcile (use in demos as "the math is on the screen")

- Segment occupancy rolls up both ways to the property's 62.5 percent (screen 07).
- Best spread: Private Bath $310 minus Shared Bath $238 = $72 (screens 06, 07).
- Forecast: $282 x 1.0 rooms x 89.5% x 4.35 weeks = $1,098 (screen 14). Scenarios are $988 and $1,207, plus and minus 10 percent.
- Visual comp medians: $245 per week and 9.5 days to fill (screen 08).

## Third-party surfaces in the product

Leaflet, OpenStreetMap, and CARTO for maps; FEMA NFHL as a toggle; a geocoder (provider unknown); a generative image model and an image-embedding model (vendors unknown). Compliance notes for each: `reference/trust-and-risk.md`.

<<<END reference/product-surface.md>>>

# Feature matrix, what leads and what is table stakes

Load for: deciding which capability a page, demo, or post should lead with. Distills: S3 feature classification. Status is owned by `rules/feature-status.md`; the role column here is a WORKING hypothesis until scoring on demand and competitiveness is done (OPEN).

Roles: **LEAD** differentiating and SHIPPED, **HOOK** fast first answer for top of funnel, **STAKE** expected, must work, **SUPPORT** strengthens a lead, **HOLD** do not feature until status or evidence changes.

| ID | Feature | Stage | Status | Role | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C01 | Market search and selection | Discover | SHIPPED | STAKE | Every market tool has it |
| C02 | Market ranking by Market Score | Discover | PARTIAL | HOOK | National leaderboard is a natural entry point; publishing it needs data rights |
| C03 | Seasonality analysis | Discover | SHIPPED | SUPPORT | Room-level fill speed by season is uncommon |
| C04 | Market forecasts | Discover | UNVERIFIED | HOLD | Output never seen |
| C05 | Submarket demand map | Discover | SHIPPED | SUPPORT | Evidence-adjusted bands show where data is thin |
| C06 | Supply map with listing status | Discover | SHIPPED | STAKE | Maps are expected |
| C07 | Flood-risk overlay | Discover | UNVERIFIED | HOLD | Toggle only |
| C08 | Market filters | Discover | UNVERIFIED | HOLD | Never opened |
| C09 | Saved views | Discover | UNVERIFIED | HOLD | Never opened |
| C10 | Market report export | Discover | UNVERIFIED | HOLD | Button looked disabled |
| C11 | Property search | Analyze | SHIPPED | STAKE | Expected |
| C12 | Property performance and revenue | Analyze | SHIPPED | SUPPORT | Room-level KPIs with a revenue disclaimer |
| C13 | Property signal and recommendation | Analyze | SHIPPED | SUPPORT | A verdict plus a next action; one label seen |
| C14 | Room-segment economics | Analyze | SHIPPED | LEAD | Bath and size premiums are the room-level insight |
| C15 | Rolling performance windows | Analyze | SHIPPED | SUPPORT | Direction and stability over 7, 30, 90 days |
| C16 | Evidence quality scoring | Analyze | PARTIAL | SUPPORT | Backs the transparency message |
| C17 | Visual comps | Analyze | SHIPPED | LEAD | Prices a room against rooms that look like it; watch D-Q18 |
| C18 | AI upgrade concepts | Analyze | SHIPPED | HOLD | Demos well, but no upgrade economics yet |
| C19 | Property trends | Analyze | UNVERIFIED | HOLD | Never opened |
| C20 | Room-level history | Analyze | UNVERIFIED | HOLD | Never opened |
| C21 | Nearby supply check | Underwrite | SHIPPED | HOOK | Instant answer for any address |
| C22 | Bedroom layout recommendation | Underwrite | UNVERIFIED | HOLD | Output never seen |
| C23 | Amenity ROI shortlist | Underwrite | UNVERIFIED | HOLD | Output never seen |
| C24 | House rules checklist | Underwrite | UNVERIFIED | HOLD | Output never seen; fair-housing review needed |
| C25 | Per-room rent guidance | Underwrite | UNVERIFIED | HOLD | Likely LEAD once verified |
| C26 | Cohort lease-up outcomes | Underwrite | UNVERIFIED | HOLD | Likely LEAD once verified |
| C27 | Revenue forecast for any address | Underwrite | SHIPPED | LEAD | Formula, support, confidence on screen; watch D-Q26, D-Q28 |
| C28 | Forecast stability test | Underwrite | SHIPPED | SUPPORT | Lets the investor stress the evidence window |
| C29 | Comp set review | Underwrite | UNVERIFIED | HOLD | Collapsed in capture |
| C30 | Garage conversion scenario | Underwrite | UNVERIFIED | HOLD | Likely HOOK once verified |
| C31 | Deal calculator | Decide | PARTIAL | STAKE | Common elsewhere; Pro gate; watch D-Q30, D-Q31 |
| C32 | Saved underwrites with re-run | Monitor | PARTIAL | SUPPORT | Retention loop once outputs are seen |

## Reading the matrix

- Three LEADs today: C14, C17, C27. Every investor asset leads with C27; every operator asset leads with C14 or C17.
- Four likely promotions after founder verification: C25, C26 to LEAD, C30 to HOOK, C29 to SUPPORT. Each needs a status AMEND first.
- C18 stays HOLD for messaging even though it is SHIPPED, because a concept image without economics invites the "boost rent by" claim that `rules/do-not-say.md` bans.

## Next analytical step (OPEN)
Score each feature 1 to 5 on demand (from design-partner signals, `innovation/experiments.md` EXP-001) and competitiveness (from `reference/competitive-analysis.md`). Record the scores here with the date and the evidence count behind each.

<<<FILE reference/icp-personas.md>>>

# ICP and personas

Load for: targeting, audience choice, sales prep, persona-specific copy. Distills: S2 working notes section 1 (ICP candidates) and the product flow in S1. All personas are WORKING (D-07) until the founder answers G05 and the design-partner program (EXP-001) reports.

## Audience A, acquiring investors (primary)

**Who.** Individual investors and small teams (one to five people) buying or converting single-family homes and townhouses into rent-by-the-room properties, in US Sun Belt metros first.

**Trigger moments.** A house under contract or in diligence. Entering a new metro. Deciding whether to convert a garage. A lender asking for a revenue basis on a DSCR loan.

**Jobs to be done.**
1. Pick a market worth buying in.
2. Check how much coliving supply already sits near an address.
3. Estimate stabilized monthly revenue room by room.
4. Decide the room mix: bathrooms, garage, common space.
5. See whether the deal still works with financing.
6. Keep the underwrite and re-check it later.

**What they use today.** A spreadsheet with typed-in room rents, a marketplace's host calculator, forum threads, a coach's rule of thumb.

**What wins them.** Seeing room-level evidence for their own address, with the uncertainty labeled. The math reproducing on screen.

**What blocks them.** "Where does the data come from?" "How accurate is it?" A first run on an uncovered address that returns a fallback forecast with Low confidence.

## Audience B, operating hosts (secondary)

**Who.** Operators running roughly one to twenty rent-by-the-room houses, often self-managed, who price rooms weekly and fight vacancy.

**Trigger moments.** A room sits empty past its usual fill time. Planning a refresh. Setting the price for a newly added room. Comparing two of their own houses.

**Jobs to be done.**
1. See which rooms earn a premium and why (bath, size).
2. Price a room from rooms that look like it.
3. Watch direction over 7, 30, and 90 days.
4. Decide which upgrade is worth doing.

**What wins them.** A best spread or a visual comp that changes a price this week.

**What blocks them.** Not seeing their own property tracked. Distrust of AI images. Price sensitivity (OPEN, G07).

## Not a GTM audience yet

Lenders, brokers, and acquisition analysts. The product serves them indirectly (DSCR, Evidence Quality), but they need a published backtest before RoomIQ can make the claims they would require. No assets for them until a decision entry changes this.

## Buying committee, Audience A

| Role | Who | Cares about | Asset that reaches them |
|---|---|---|---|
| Decider and payer | The investor | Will this deal work, fast | Live demo on their address |
| Approver | Spouse, JV partner, capital partner | Downside, evidence | Exported underwrite (C32, PARTIAL) |
| Influencer | DSCR or portfolio lender | Revenue basis, method | Methodology one-pager, no accuracy claims |
| Influencer | Coach or community | Tool credibility for students | Education series, community posts |
| Later user | Operator or property manager | Pricing, occupancy | Analyzer walkthrough |

## Design-partner profile
An Audience A investor with at least one live deal in a covered metro, willing to run it through the Predictor on a call and tell the founder what they decided and why. Ten of them is the first experiment (EXP-001).

## Segments to watch in the signal log
- Conversion specialists (garage, basement) once C30 is verified.
- Out-of-state investors buying Sun Belt houses remotely, who lack local knowledge.
- Operators scaling past ten houses, who may need team features (none seen).

<<<END reference/icp-personas.md>>>


<<<FILE reference/positioning.md>>>

# Positioning

Load for: homepage, pitch, one-liners, category questions. Distills: master context Sections 5, 7, 12. Status: WORKING (D-08, D-09) until founder sign-off.

## Category
Room-level market intelligence and underwriting, for US rent-by-the-room housing.

## Positioning statement
For US rent-by-the-room investors deciding where to buy, what a house will earn, and how to price its rooms, RoomIQ is room-level market intelligence and underwriting that shows its evidence. Short-term rental analytics model nightly stays and rent comps model whole units; RoomIQ works in the unit this business runs on, the room, priced weekly. And where a spreadsheet hides its guesses, every RoomIQ forecast prints its formula, its comps, and how much to trust it.

## The three things RoomIQ leads on
1. **The room is the unit.** Weekly room rents, room occupancy, fill speed, and bath and size segments (C14, C15, C12).
2. **Evidence you can see.** Formula printed, support labeled, comp distance disclosed, confidence labeled (C27, C28, C16).
3. **Rooms that look alike.** Visual comps with weekly price and days to fill (C17).

## Reframes, in order of use
- From "What will this house rent for?" to "What will each room earn, and how sure can I be?"
- From "a confident number" to "a number that tells you how far to trust it".
- From "comps nearby" to "rooms that look like yours, wherever they are".

## One-liners (checked against ledgers, founder approval pending)

| Length | Line |
|---|---|
| 5 words | Underwrite the room, not just the house. |
| 10 words | Room-level market data and forecasts for rent-by-the-room investors. |
| 25 words | RoomIQ forecasts what each room in a US house can earn, from observed weekly room rents and occupancy, and shows its formula, comps, and confidence. |

## What positioning must not drift into
- An accuracy story (D-05).
- A data-scale story (no coverage numbers, G13).
- An "AI underwriting" story. AI framing belongs only to visual comps and AI concepts (G19).
- A short-term rental story. Different unit, different buyer.
- A marketplace story. RoomIQ lists nothing and books nothing.

## Defensibility, internal only
Room-level history compounds with time: every observed day deepens the evidence behind scores and forecasts. The transparency posture is hard to retrofit onto tools built around one confident number. Neither point is a public claim until coverage and history depth are confirmed (G13).

<<<END reference/positioning.md>>>


<<<FILE reference/value-proposition-investors.md>>>

# Value proposition, acquiring investors

Load for: any asset whose audience is Audience A. Never mix with `value-proposition-operators.md` in one asset. Distills: master context Section 10. Status: WORKING (D-07).

## Brand promise
Know what each room can earn before you buy the house, and how much to trust the number.

## Positioning for this audience
You already know rent-by-the-room economics live or die on the room. RoomIQ gives you room-level evidence for any US address, and where nearby evidence is thin it labels the forecast fallback support with its confidence, so a deal decision rests on observed rents instead of a guess in a spreadsheet.

## Pillar 1, find the market
**Headline options:** "Start where rooms fill." / "See which US markets rank highest before you look at a single house."
**Reasons to believe (SHIPPED or PARTIAL only):**
- Choose up to 3 US cities, ZIPs, or a metro group per dashboard (C01).
- Top US markets ranked by a 0 to 100 Market Score with a letter grade (C02, PARTIAL: name it, do not explain inputs).
- Seasonality of occupancy and fill speed, with the national pattern labeled when local data is thin (C03).
- A submarket map that bands cells Strong, Watch, Weak, or Thin, evidence-adjusted (C05).

## Pillar 2, underwrite at the room level
**Headline options:** "Underwrite the room, not just the house." / "A forecast that shows its work."
**Reasons to believe:**
- Underwrite any US address. Where nearby evidence is thin, RoomIQ labels the forecast fallback support and shows its confidence (C27).
- The formula prints under the number: price times rooms times occupancy times 4.35 weeks (C27).
- See nearby coliving supply within about 3 miles before you run anything (C21).
- Test the forecast against a shorter or longer evidence window (C28).
- Bathroom mix and room mix are first-class inputs, because private-bath supply drives revenue (FACT, baseline profile copy).

## Pillar 3, decide with the financing math
**Headline options:** "Carry the forecast into the deal." / "From room revenue to DSCR in one flow."
**Reasons to believe (PARTIAL, describe inputs only):**
- On RoomIQ Pro, the Deal Calculator prefills monthly room revenue from the forecast and takes your purchase and financing inputs, for cash flow, CoC, DSCR, and cap rate (C31). For information, not financial advice.
- Saved underwrites appear in My Underwrites for re-running later (C32).

## What we never promise this audience
Accuracy, returns, a "good deal", lender acceptance, legal approval of a conversion, or data from any named source.

## Copy lengths

| Length | Copy |
|---|---|
| Headline | Underwrite the room, not just the house. |
| Subhead | Room-level revenue forecasts with the formula, the comps, and the confidence on screen. |
| Paragraph | Pick an address. RoomIQ checks nearby coliving supply, takes your room and bathroom mix, and forecasts monthly revenue from observed weekly room rents and occupancy. The formula prints under the number, and when local evidence is thin it says fallback support and shows a confidence label, so you know how far to trust it before you make an offer. |

## Proof
Customer proof: none on file. Use `[PROOF POINT NEEDED]` where a story would go. Product facts from `ops/copy-bank.md` only.

<<<END reference/value-proposition-investors.md>>>


<<<FILE reference/value-proposition-operators.md>>>

# Value proposition, operating hosts

Load for: any asset whose audience is Audience B. Never mix with `value-proposition-investors.md` in one asset. Distills: master context Section 11. Status: WORKING (D-07).

## Brand promise
See how every room in your house earns against rooms like it.

## Positioning for this audience
You price rooms weekly and feel every empty one. RoomIQ shows which of your rooms earn a premium, how similar-looking rooms are priced and how fast they fill, and how your property is trending, so a pricing change rests on evidence.

## Pillar 1, benchmark at the room level
**Headline options:** "Find the room that earns your premium." / "Your house, room by room."
**Reasons to believe (SHIPPED):**
- A Property Signal with a plain-language recommendation for each property (C13).
- Room segments by bathroom (Private, Shared) and size (Cozy, Standard), each with average weekly price and 90-day occupancy (C14).
- The best spread between segments, for example a $72 per week bathroom premium in one Austin capture (C14).
- Rolling 7, 30, and 90-day windows: occupancy, daily price, volatility, and change against the prior window (C15).

## Pillar 2, price from rooms that look like yours
**Headline options:** "Rooms that look like yours, and what they rent for." / "Price against the room, not the zip code."
**Reasons to believe (SHIPPED):**
- Visually Similar Rooms finds rooms whose photos match yours, with each one's weekly price and days to fill, plus the medians (C17).
- Click any match to open that property (C17).

## Pillar 3, plan upgrades with eyes open
**Headline options:** "See an upgrade before you buy the paint." / "Preview the desk before you buy it."
**Reasons to believe:**
- Media Studio generates an AI concept of an upgrade on your listing photo, side by side with the original, from presets such as Add desk, Repaint neutral, and LVP flooring (C18, SHIPPED).
- Every concept is watermarked "AI-GENERATED - NOT ACTUAL PROPERTY CONDITION" (FACT).
- Amenity ROI and per-room rent guidance exist in the Property Predictor (C23, C25, UNVERIFIED: name only).
- No validated upgrade economics yet. Say so.

## What we never promise this audience
Higher rent from an upgrade, faster fill, more bookings, or that their own property is tracked.

## Copy lengths

| Length | Copy |
|---|---|
| Headline | Find the room that earns your premium. |
| Subhead | Room-level benchmarks, visual comps, and rolling windows for rent-by-the-room operators. |
| Paragraph | RoomIQ breaks a property into its rooms: private bath versus shared, cozy versus standard, each with its weekly price and 90-day occupancy. It shows rooms elsewhere that look like yours, with what they rent for and how fast they filled, so your next price change starts from evidence. |

## Proof
Customer proof: none on file. `[PROOF POINT NEEDED]`.

# Customer journey funnels

Load for: matching an asset to a stage, choosing KPIs, planning onboarding. Distills: master context Section 13. Status: WORKING. KPI baselines: not measured yet (`innovation/metrics.md`).

## Investor funnel (Audience A)

| Stage | Mindset | Question they ask | Asset | KPI (baseline pending) | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Unaware | Running deals on gut and spreadsheets | none | none | none | none |
| 2 Problem aware | "My room rent assumptions are guesses" | How do others underwrite rooms? | Education post, community answer | Engaged readers from ICP | Founder |
| 3 Solution aware | "Room-level evidence exists" | What tools do this? | "Underwrite the room" article, walkthrough video | Visits to the product page | Founder |
| 4 Evaluating | "Will it work on my deal?" | Does it cover my market? How sure is it? | Live demo on their address, trial | Demo-to-trial rate | Founder |
| 5 Activated | "This changed how I see the deal" | Can I trust this enough to act? | First forecast in a covered market, then the Deal Calculator | Activation rate, time to first forecast | Product |
| 6 Habit | Running every candidate deal through it | Can I keep these? | My Underwrites, re-run | Forecasts per active user per week | Product |
| 7 Paid | RoomIQ Pro for the Deal Calculator | Is Pro worth it? | Upgrade prompt at the Deal Calculator | Trial-to-paid rate | Founder |
| 8 Advocate | Sends it to a JV partner | Can I share this? | Exported underwrite | Referred signups | Founder |

**Activation definition (hypothesis A1, tested in EXP-001):** a forecast run on an address in a covered metro that returns better than Low confidence, followed by opening the Deal Calculator in the same session.

**Critical success factor:** the first forecast lands in a covered market.
**Primary blocker:** a first run on an uncovered address (D-Q28), or the data-source question going unanswered.
**Accelerator:** the founder running the prospect's own address live.

## Operator funnel (Audience B)

| Stage | Mindset | Question | Asset | KPI (baseline pending) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Unaware | Pricing by feel | none | none | none |
| 2 Problem aware | "A room keeps sitting empty" | What are similar rooms charging? | Community answer, pricing article | ICP engagement |
| 3 Solution aware | "Room-level benchmarks exist" | Is my house in there? | Analyzer walkthrough | Product page visits |
| 4 Evaluating | "Show me my property" | How does my house compare? | Analyzer on a comparable property, visual comps | Searches per trial |
| 5 Activated | "That premium explains it" | What should I change? | Segment premium or visual comp that changes a price | Price changes reported |
| 6 Habit | Weekly check | Which way is it trending? | Rolling windows | Weekly active operators |
| 7 Paid | Pro (OPEN) | Is it worth it? | Upgrade prompt | Trial-to-paid |
| 8 Advocate | Tells their operator group | none | Shareable benchmark | Referrals |

## Stage rules for writers
- Stages 2 and 3: no product claims beyond one line. Teach first.
- Stage 4: product only, one audience, covered markets only.
- Stage 5 onward: in-product copy and lifecycle email. Glossary terms exactly as in the UI.

<<<FILE reference/competitive-analysis.md>>>

# Competitive market analysis

Load for: competitive questions, comparison pages, "how is this different from X". Distills: S7 desk scan of public pages, 2026-11-13. Every rival fact below is from the rival's or a third party's public page on that date. Re-verify before any external use, and record the re-check date here.

## Market shape
There is no established category of room-level investor analytics. Rent-by-the-room investors assemble a view from five alternatives plus the status quo.

| Alternative | Representative tools | Built for | Unit of analysis | Where it stops for this buyer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Status quo | Spreadsheets, forums, coaches | Anyone | Whatever the investor types | No market evidence behind the room rent assumption |
| Platform-native host tools | Marketplace host dashboards, earnings calculators, market reports | That platform's own hosts | Room, inside one platform | One platform's view; self-reported; built for hosts already on it |
| Short-term rental analytics | AirDNA, Mashvisor, Rabbu | Airbnb-style hosts and investors | Night | Nightly stays, not weekly room rents |
| Whole-unit rent comps | Rentometer, HelloData, RentCast | Landlords, multifamily, brokers | Unit | Whole units, not rooms |
| Deal calculators | DealCheck and similar | Buy-and-hold investors | Deal | Revenue is an assumption the user types |
| Data vendors and research | SFR Analytics (room-for-rent analysis), operator reports | Analysts | Varies | Research and data feeds, not an underwriting workflow |

## Scoring vectors (WORKING)
1. **Granularity.** Room, unit, or night.
2. **Evidence transparency.** Does the output show its formula, support, and confidence?
3. **Underwriting depth.** Address to forecast to financed returns in one flow.
4. **Visual evidence.** Photo-based comps.
5. **Coverage independence.** Breadth across sources and markets. OPEN for RoomIQ (G11, G13), so never claimed.

## Where RoomIQ sits (WORKING, unscored)
- Strong on vectors 1 to 4 as SHIPPED capabilities.
- Unknown on vector 5. Do not compete on it.
- Weak where rivals have depth RoomIQ cannot claim: years of history (AirDNA), API ecosystems (Rentometer, HelloData), and the platforms' first-party booking data.

## The wedge
Room-level evidence plus visible uncertainty. Rivals either work at the wrong unit or leave the revenue assumption to the investor. RoomIQ starts from observed room rents and says how far to trust the result.

## Public facts gathered (2026-11-13, re-verify before use)
- A leading marketplace's host tools show each room's price against the metro average and a market insights map; the marketplace publishes monthly market reports and an earnings calculator. Its occupancy data is self-reported from its own bookings.
- AirDNA is a short-term rental data platform, widely cited as the default for STR market research.
- Mashvisor is positioned on comparing short-term and long-term rental strategies on one property.
- Rabbu offers short-term rental tools free and runs a property marketplace.
- Rentometer offers address-level rent estimates and an API built on whole-unit inputs (bedrooms, bathrooms, building type).
- HelloData offers multifamily rent comps and a rent comps API, including concession tracking.
- DealCheck analyzes buy-and-hold, rehab, Airbnb, and vacation rentals; coliving is not listed as a property type.
- SFR Analytics published an analysis of room-for-rent listings against whole-home rent estimates; it is research, not a room-level product.

## Open competitive questions
- Is there a direct room-level investor analytics product in this market? None found in the scan. Absence of evidence is not a claim: never write "the only".
- What do the marketplaces' host tools show non-hosts, if anything?
- Who do design partners name when asked "what else did you look at?" (EXP-001 captures this).

<<<END reference/competitive-analysis.md>>>


<<<FILE reference/competitor-battlecards.md>>>

# Competitor battlecards

Load for: sales calls, objection prep, comparison copy. Distills: `reference/competitive-analysis.md`. Three lines per rival: their real strength first, their real gap, how RoomIQ wins. Rival facts dated 2026-11-13; re-verify before external use.

Rule: lead with the rival's genuine strength. A card that pretends a rival is weak loses the room the moment the prospect knows better.

## The status quo: spreadsheet plus forums
- **Strength.** Free, fully flexible, and the investor trusts their own assumptions.
- **Gap.** The room rent and occupancy inputs are guesses; nothing shows how sure the investor should be.
- **How RoomIQ wins.** Run their address live. Show the forecast with the formula, the comps, and the confidence label, then let them compare it to the number in their sheet.

## Platform-native host tools (a marketplace's own dashboard and calculator)
- **Strength.** First-party booking data for that platform's rooms, free to its hosts, and integrated with how they already operate.
- **Gap.** One platform's view, built for hosts already on it, self-reported. An investor evaluating a house they do not own yet is not the primary user.
- **How RoomIQ wins.** Underwrite any US address before the purchase, with room-level evidence and fallback support labeled where nearby evidence is thin. Never claim independence from any platform or name a data source (D-04).

## AirDNA
- **Strength.** Deep short-term rental data and wide recognition as the STR research default.
- **Gap.** Built for nightly stays. Weekly room rents, room occupancy, and fill speed are not its model.
- **How RoomIQ wins.** "AirDNA is built for nightly stays. RoomIQ models weekly room rents and room occupancy." Never "better than AirDNA".

## Mashvisor
- **Strength.** Compares short-term and long-term strategies on the same property, investor-oriented workflow.
- **Gap.** Rent-by-the-room is not one of the strategies it is known for.
- **How RoomIQ wins.** For an investor already set on rent-by-the-room, RoomIQ works at the room level from the first screen.

## Rabbu
- **Strength.** Free short-term rental tools.
- **Gap.** Short-term rental focus.
- **How RoomIQ wins.** Different unit, different decision. Do not compete on price (pricing OPEN).

## Rentometer, HelloData, RentCast
- **Strength.** Address-level rent comps and mature APIs; HelloData tracks concessions in multifamily.
- **Gap.** Whole units. A rent-by-the-room house earns from rooms with different bath and size mixes.
- **How RoomIQ wins.** Room segments and best spread: show that a private-bath room and a shared-bath room in the same house earn differently ($310 vs $238 per week in screen 07).

## DealCheck and similar calculators
- **Strength.** Mature deal math: cash flow, CoC, DSCR, cap rate, multiple strategies.
- **Gap.** Revenue is typed by the user; coliving is not a listed property type.
- **How RoomIQ wins.** The Deal Calculator starts from the RoomIQ forecast instead of a guess (C31, PARTIAL: show inputs prefilled, do not show outputs until captured).

## What to never say about any rival
Rumors, pricing you have not verified this month, "they scrape", "their data is wrong", or any claim about a rival's roadmap.

<<<END reference/competitor-battlecards.md>>>


<<<FILE reference/objection-handling.md>>>

# Objection handling

Load for: sales calls, FAQ sections, support replies, community answers. Distills: S2 open questions and QA issues, the claim ledger, and the battlecards. Where the honest answer is "not yet", it says not yet. Add new objections from `ops/signal-log.md` when a WATCH reaches its threshold.

## "Where does your data come from?"
Honest answer today: "RoomIQ is built from observed room listings in the markets it covers, tracked over time at the room level. Every metric shows its as-of date, and every property shows an Evidence Quality score so you can see how complete the history is."
Never name or imply a source, a partner, or a collection method (D-04). If pushed: "I'll get you a written answer on sourcing" and log the signal as OBJECTION.

## "How accurate is the forecast?"
"We don't claim accuracy yet. What you get instead is the forecast's working: the formula, the number of comps, how far away they are, whether local evidence was enough, and a confidence label. On a thin-evidence address it will tell you that, in red."
If the founder publishes a backtest (G14), this answer changes by AMEND.

## "Does it cover my market?"
"Run your address and RoomIQ shows nearby coliving supply within about three miles first. If evidence is thin, the forecast says fallback support and shows its confidence." In a live call, choose the address yourself only in covered metros (D-06).

## "My house isn't on any platform yet. Does that matter?"
"No. The Property Predictor underwrites any US address from your baseline profile: type, bedrooms, bathrooms, room mix, and if nearby evidence is thin the forecast says fallback support. Tracked properties use their own history; new ones use the bounded underwriting path."

## "Why not just use AirDNA?"
"AirDNA is built for nightly stays. A rent-by-the-room house earns weekly, room by room, and its rooms earn differently by bathroom and size. RoomIQ models that unit."

## "I already have a spreadsheet."
"Keep it. Put RoomIQ's forecast next to your room rent assumption and see where they differ, with the comps behind the difference."

## "Are the AI images real?"
"No, and the product says so on every one: AI-generated, not actual property condition, watermarked into the downloaded file. They are concepts for planning, with no validated rent impact yet."

## "Can I give this to my lender?"
"You can share the underwrite as your own analysis. RoomIQ isn't a lender product or an appraisal, and the Deal Calculator is for information, not financial advice." Do not say "lender-ready".

## "What does it cost?"
Pricing is not decided (D-11). Say: "I'll send current plans after the call." Never quote a number.

## "Is rent-by-the-room legal where I'm buying?"
"RoomIQ compares an operating checklist with recorded local policies, but it isn't legal advice. Check local occupancy and rooming-house rules with someone qualified." House rules output is UNVERIFIED (C24): do not describe it.

## "What does Market Score measure?"
"It's a 0 to 100 score with a letter grade that ranks markets for this model." Do not list inputs until G18 is answered.

<<<END reference/objection-handling.md>>>

# Marketing campaigns and asset backlog

Load for: planning what to produce next, and why. Distills: master context Section 14. Status: WORKING (D-10). Each campaign names the assumption it tests, because every campaign is also an experiment (`innovation/experiments.md`).

## Campaign 1, design-partner program (priority now)

**Goal:** ten investors in covered metros run a live deal through the Predictor with the founder.
**Assets:**

**Audience:** A. **Stage:** 2 to 3. **Tests:** G1 via EXP-004.
**Topics, one per piece:**
- Why room mix beats bedroom count in rent-by-the-room underwriting.
- Shared-bath pressure: rooms per shared bathroom and why it matters.
- Fill speed versus occupancy: two different risks.

- DSCR for room rentals: what a lender reads from your revenue basis.
**Assets:** SEO article, social post, short walkthrough video per topic (`templates/seo-article.md`, `templates/social-post.md`).

## Campaign 4, operator benchmarking
**Audience:** B. **Stage:** 2 to 5. **Tests:** A4.
**Core idea:** "Find the room that earns your premium."
**Assets:** community answers on room pricing, an Analyzer walkthrough on a comparable property, a visual comps explainer.

**Blocked by:** G11 and G12 (data rights). **Tests:** G1, R1.
**When unblocked:** a recurring "Top US markets for rent-by-the-room" report from the Dashboard leaderboard and seasonality. Until then, no published market statistics.

Release notes, in-app microcopy, empty states, and error messages are GTM surfaces. Template: `templates/release-note.md`. The engineering backlog already holds copy fixes that the brain settles: Q14 pluralization, Q27 "has", Q33 forecast versus baseline, Q19 the empty `CONCEPT ·` label.

<<<FILE reference/content-engine.md>>>

# Content engine, education-led content

Load for: any article, post, video, or newsletter. Every content template points back here. Status: WORKING channel (D-10).

## Thesis
Rent-by-the-room investors learn from each other in public: forums, groups, podcasts, YouTube. They distrust tool marketing and trust worked examples. So RoomIQ content teaches the underwriting method first, shows the product second, and never asks for trust it has not earned with arithmetic.

## How the channels feed each other
1. Community answers surface the questions people actually ask (signal type LANGUAGE).
2. Repeated questions become articles and short videos (Campaign 2).
3. Articles carry one call to action into a demo or a trial (stage 3 to 4).
4. Demos produce objections and proof requests, which return to the signal log and sharpen the next piece.

## Archetypes to rotate
- **The worked example.** One house, one question, the numbers shown. Covered metro only.
- **The method piece.** How to think about one underwriting variable (room mix, shared-bath pressure, fill speed).
- **The myth check.** A common rule of thumb, tested against what the evidence shows. Only with numbers RoomIQ can show on screen.
- **The honest limitation.** What RoomIQ does when evidence is thin, and why the label matters.
- **The operator teardown.** Room segments of a property explained (blurred host and photos).

## Plan, write, edit
**Plan.** One reader (A or B), one stage, one question, one takeaway sentence, one call to action. Name the capability IDs you will mention and confirm their status.
**Write.** Open with the reader's question in their words (pull from `ops/copy-bank.md` customer language once it exists). Teach before you show. Every number carries its unit and window.
**Edit.** Cut the warm-up. Run `python3 tools/brain.py lint`. Check every capability against `rules/feature-status.md`. Read the opening aloud.

## Hook patterns that fit this audience
- A number with its unit: "A shared bath cost this house $72 a week per room."
- A decision: "Garage or two bedrooms? Answer this first."
- A candid limit: "This forecast came back Low confidence. Here is why that is useful."

## Calls to action, one per piece
- "Run your address" (stage 3 to 4).
- "Book a 30-minute underwriting session" (design partners).
- "See how your house compares" (operators).

## Measurement
Per piece: ICP engagement (replies, saves, qualified comments), clicks to the one CTA, demos booked. A piece succeeds on its role, not on views. Log each published piece in `ops/activity-log.md` with the experiment it serves.

## Out of scope
Paid promotion, cold outreach at volume, and any published market statistics until G11 and G12 are answered.

<<<END reference/content-engine.md>>>


<<<FILE reference/demo-playbook.md>>>

# Demo playbook, founder-led demos

Load for: live demos, recorded walkthroughs, screenshots for any public surface. This is the second channel engine: demos are where status discipline breaks first. Distills: S1 screens 01 to 15, S2 QA issues, D-06.

## The demo path (covered metro, about 20 minutes)
1. **Dashboard.** Choose a Sun Belt metro preset. Show Top US markets by Market Score and the Explore map bands. Say what "Thin" means: too little evidence, not weak demand.
2. **Drawer.** Open a property. Read the revenue disclaimer aloud: "Based on observed rents and occupancy, not collected payments."
3. **Analyzer.** Property Signal, room segments, best spread, rolling windows. Do the arithmetic out loud: segment occupancy reconciles to the property.
4. **Visual comps.** Scroll past any non-bedroom photo without comment; never make one a talking point (D-Q18).
5. **Predictor.** Use an address in Dallas, Austin, Houston, Atlanta, Phoenix, or Tampa that you have tested that day. Show nearby supply, complete the room mix fully (avoids D-Q26), run the forecast, read the formula, the support level, and the confidence label aloud.
6. **Deal Calculator.** Type every input yourself, including the interest rate. Never show defaults (D-Q30, D-Q31). Say "for information, not financial advice".
7. **Close.** Offer to run the prospect's own address, if it is in a covered metro.

## Landmines, never on screen

| Defect | What happens | Avoid by |
|---|---|---|
| D-Q26 | Banner says full bedroom count; math uses 1.0 active rooms | Entering every room in Room Mix before running |
| D-Q28, D-Q29 | Uncovered address forecasts on comps 80+ miles away | Pre-tested covered addresses only |
| D-Q30, D-Q31 | Interest default may read 22%; vacancy may double count | Typing all inputs |
| D-Q18 | Closet photos in visual comps | Not dwelling on the grid |
| Q11 | Most DFW cells are Thin, the map looks empty | Zooming to a dense cluster |
| Q16 | A typo in Analyzer search matches title text | Typing city names exactly |

## Never shown as if a customer can use it today
Every UNVERIFIED capability: Forecasts tab, filters, views, report export, Trends and Rooms tabs, layouts, amenity ROI, house rules, rent guidance, cohorts, comp review, garage conversion compare. Clicking one live is allowed only if it was tested that day and the output is captured afterwards for a status AMEND.

## Public screenshots and recordings
- Blur host names and third-party listing photos until G12 is answered.
- AI concepts keep the watermark visible.
- No account email or avatar in frame.

## After every demo
Log within 24 hours: one activity in `ops/activity-log.md`, and every objection, phrase, or request in `ops/signal-log.md` with the verbatim. A demo that logs nothing taught the brain nothing.

<<<END reference/demo-playbook.md>>>


<<<FILE reference/trust-and-risk.md>>>

# Trust and risk register

Load for: legal-adjacent copy, disclaimers, sourcing questions, AI disclosures, financial outputs, house rules, and reviewing anything a regulator, platform, or lender might read. Distills: S2 working notes section 7 (dependencies) and section 9 (QA). This is not legal advice; it is the list of exposures the copy must respect until counsel reviews them.

## Exposures, ranked by consequence

| # | Exposure | Why it matters | Copy rule today | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | Listing data provenance and terms | Core to the product and to any public statistic | Never name or imply a source or partner | G11 |
| T2 | Third-party listing photos and host names on screen | Rights to display; privacy | Blur in public assets | G12 |
| T3 | AI derivatives of listing photos | Copyright and platform rules on altered photos; deceptive advertising | Concepts always watermarked and labeled; never used as listing photos | G12 |
| T4 | Forecast and financial outputs | Investors and lenders act on them | No accuracy claims; "for information, not financial advice" on every financial surface | G14 |
| T5 | House rules recommendations | Fair housing; local occupancy and rooming-house law | No protected-class references; "not legal advice" | C24 UNVERIFIED |
| T6 | FEMA flood layer | Misread as an insurance determination | "Not an insurance or regulatory determination" | C07 UNVERIFIED |
| T7 | Map tiles and geocoding at scale | Commercial terms of basemap and geocoder providers | Keep OpenStreetMap attribution visible | Provider unknown |
| T8 | Privacy choices and consent | US state privacy laws | Do not describe privacy features beyond the link | B8 |

## Verbatim disclosures already in the product (keep exactly)
- Revenue: "Based on observed rents and occupancy, not collected payments."
- AI concept banner: "AI-GENERATED - NOT ACTUAL PROPERTY CONDITION"
- AI concept economics: "Concept visualization" with "no validated economics for this edit yet."
- Scenarios: "Revenue assumptions, not a calibrated prediction interval."
- Map: "Market metrics only count live listings."
The full AI disclaimer sentence is quoted in `rules/do-not-say.md`.

## Disclosures the brain adds to marketing surfaces
- Deal math: "For information, not financial advice."
- House rules: "Not legal advice. Confirm local rules."
- Any forecast in marketing: the fallback clause and the confidence label, together.

## Trust assets RoomIQ already has (use them)
The product's own candor is the strongest trust asset: printed formulas, labeled support and confidence, disclosed comp distance, separated local and expanded comps, excluded soft signals, reconciling numbers, watermarking. Lead with them; never oversell past them.

## Fair housing note for every writer
Rent-by-the-room listings often carry house rules. RoomIQ copy never suggests rules or resident criteria tied to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, disability, or state-protected classes such as source of income. If a generated house-rule recommendation ever contains one, log it as a RISK signal immediately (threshold: 1 verified instance).

<<<END reference/trust-and-risk.md>>>

# Pricing and packaging, hypotheses only

Load for: packaging discussions, paywall copy, upgrade prompts. Distills: S2 working notes section 6. Pricing is OPEN (D-11). Nothing in this file may appear in external copy except the two FACT lines.

## FACT, visible in the product
- A plan named `RoomIQ Pro` exists (badge, top right).
- The Deal Calculator is marked Pro. The chips "Unlimited analyzer access" and "Unlimited baseline runs" appear on a Pro account.

## Signals, and what each suggests (hypotheses)

| Signal seen | Suggests | Packaging lever | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| "Unlimited analyzer access" | Analyzer use is metered on a lower tier | Analyses per month | A3, pricing interviews |
| "Unlimited baseline runs" | Predictor runs are metered on a lower tier | Forecasts per month | A3 |
| Deal Calculator marked Pro | The clearest gating line in the product | Pro-only decision tools | EXP-003 |
| Up to 3 cities per dashboard | Possibly a tier lever | Markets per dashboard | Ask founder (G07) |
| Market Report download | Export as a premium feature | Report exports | C10 UNVERIFIED |
| Media Studio | Compute cost per generation | Credits or an add-on | Ask founder |
| My Underwrites with re-run | Retention and upsell | Saved-report limits, future alerts | A7 |

## Packaging principles to propose to the founder (not decided)
1. Gate decisions, not discovery: free or low tier sees markets and a forecast; Pro gets the Deal Calculator and saved underwrites. Matches the visible Pro badge.
2. Meter what costs money: AI concept generations.
3. Never gate the trust labels. Support, confidence, and formulas show on every tier, because they are the positioning.

## Copy rules until pricing is decided
- Upgrade prompts say what Pro adds, never what it costs.
- No trial lengths, no "free forever", no discounts, no annual savings.
- "See current plans" links are fine once a pricing page exists (B2 in coverage gaps).
