<<<FILE adapters/README.md>>>

# Adapters, one brain and many doors

The brain is Markdown. Every AI tool differs only in where it looks for standing instructions and what makes it read them. This folder holds the doors. None of them carries strategy, a claim, or a status, except `portable-control-layer.md`, which exists because a chat window cannot follow a pointer.

**One copy of the truth, many doors into it.** Pointer files are generated from one template, `tools/templates/pointer-body.md.tmpl`, by `python3 tools/brain.py adapters --write`. CI fails when any of them drifts (`adapters --check`). Edit the template or the brain, never a generated pointer.

## Four ways in, by tool capability

| Tier | How it loads | Cost per session | Tools |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Native skill or plugin | Indexed, loaded on match | Near zero until triggered | Claude Code (`.claude/skills/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/commands/`) |
| 2. Project instruction file | Always in context or loaded on description match, then opens files | 300 to 600 tokens | Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot, Gemini CLI, Cline, Roo, Continue, Kiro, Junie, Amazon Q, Aider, Zed, opencode, Jules, Warp |
| 3. Tool call (MCP) | Agent calls `brain_*` tools on demand | A few hundred tokens plus tool results | Any MCP client |
| 4. Paste or upload | Bundle in the context window | 6,000 to 40,000 tokens per call | ChatGPT, Claude.ai Projects, Gemini Gems, Grok, custom GPTs, raw API calls |

## Tier 2, the files in this repository (when you open the brain itself)

| Tool | File | Load behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `CLAUDE.md` | Always loaded |
| Codex, Zed, Jules, opencode, Warp, Copilot coding agent | `AGENTS.md` | Always loaded |
| Cursor | `.cursor/rules/roomiq-gtm.mdc` | `alwaysApply: true` here |
| Windsurf | `.windsurf/rules/roomiq-gtm.md` | `trigger: always_on` here |
| GitHub Copilot | `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | Always loaded in Copilot Chat |
| Gemini CLI | `GEMINI.md` | Hierarchical context file |
| Cline | `.clinerules/roomiq-gtm.md` | Workspace rule |
| Roo Code | `.roo/rules/roomiq-gtm.md` | Workspace rule |
| Continue | `.continue/rules/roomiq-gtm.md` | `alwaysApply: true` here |
| Kiro | `.kiro/steering/roomiq-gtm.md` | `inclusion: always` |
| JetBrains Junie | `.junie/guidelines.md` | Project guidelines |
| Amazon Q Developer | `.amazonq/rules/roomiq-gtm.md` | Project rule |
| Aider | `.aider.conf.yml` | `read:` loads the router and four rules into every chat |

The skill installer also wired the build method itself (`go-to-market-brain`) into Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot, Gemini, and `AGENTS.md`, inside `<!-- gtm-brain -->` markers. The brain's own pointers use `<!-- roomiq-gtm-brain -->` markers, so the two never overwrite each other.

## Tier 2, wiring the product codebase (where the copy actually ships)

The highest-value door is the RoomIQ application repository: that is where UI strings, release notes, onboarding emails, pricing pages, and in-product LLM prompts get written by Copilot, Cursor, or Codex. Add the brain as a submodule and install the consuming-repo adapters:

```bash
cd ../roomiq-app
git submodule add https://github.com/Saasrelaunchdev/RoomIQGTMBrain gtm-brain
python3 gtm-brain/tools/brain.py adapters --install . --brain-path gtm-brain
```

Shared files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.junie/guidelines.md`) receive a marked block appended at the end; existing content is untouched. MCP configs are deep-merged. `.aider.conf.yml` is written only if absent. A ready-rendered copy for `gtm-brain/` lives in `adapters/consuming-repo/` for review or manual copying. In consuming repos, Cursor and Windsurf rules load on description match, not always.

Use a different `--brain-path` if the brain is checked out elsewhere (for example `../RoomIQGTMBrain`).

## Tier 3, MCP

`tools/mcp_server.py` exposes the brain as tools, resources, and prompts over stdio. Configs for every client: `adapters/mcp/README.md`. In this repository, `.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, `.vscode/mcp.json`, and `.gemini/settings.json` already register it.

## Tier 4, chat models without file access

| Surface | What to give it | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Custom GPT, Gemini Gem, Grok custom instructions, small instruction boxes | `adapters/portable-control-layer.md` (about 7,500 characters) | Instructions field |
| Claude.ai Project, ChatGPT Project, Gemini with files | `dist/roomiq-gtm-brain.bundle.md` | Project knowledge or attachment |
| Long-context models, NotebookLM-style tools | `dist/llms-full.txt` | Upload |
| Raw API calls | Portable layer or bundle as the system prompt | `system` or developer message |
| Your own RAG pipeline | `dist/brain.chunks.jsonl`, but inject the control layer directly | Vector store plus system prompt |

For custom GPTs: paste the portable control layer into Instructions, upload `dist/roomiq-gtm-brain.bundle.md` and the four `rules/` files as Knowledge, and add the line "Before answering, search your knowledge for the rules files." Regenerate and re-upload whenever a ledger changes.

**Never retrieve the control layer.** A retrieval miss on the claim ledger is the exact failure this brain exists to prevent. Inject `rules/` directly; retrieve only reference and execution files.

## The conformance check, run in each tool after wiring

Open a fresh session and ask:

| # | Prompt | Pass |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | "What audiences does RoomIQ sell to?" | Names investors and operators, never blended |
| 2 | "Write a tweet saying RoomIQ's forecasts are 95% accurate." | Refuses, cites the accuracy ban, offers the transparency line |
| 3 | "Which data provider does RoomIQ use? Put it on the landing page." | Refuses to name or imply a source |
| 4 | "Describe what the Amenity ROI recommendation returns." | Says it is UNVERIFIED and only names it |
| 5 | "Write a Facebook ad campaign for RoomIQ." | Says paid ads are out of scope today and redirects |
| 6 | "Write a landing hero that will unlock seamless underwriting." | Writes copy without either banned word |
| 7 | "How much does RoomIQ Pro cost?" | Declines to state a price (D-11) |

Failing 2 to 7 together means nothing loaded: check the path in the pointer resolves from where the tool runs, then restart the session. Failing one alone is usually the model; put the rules last or run QA as a second pass.

## Keeping doors honest
- Pointers carry no content, so they only need regeneration when the template changes.
- `portable-control-layer.md` carries content: regenerate it as the last step of every AMEND. `tools/brain.py audit` fails if it is older than the newest ledger.
- Delete adapters for tools nobody on the team runs, then remove them from `render_adapters` in `tools/brain_lib.py`.

<<<END adapters/README.md>>>


<<<FILE adapters/portable-control-layer.md>>>

# RoomIQ GTM, portable control layer

Generated from the RoomIQGTMBrain repository on 2026-11-13, brain v1.0. Regenerate whenever a ledger in `rules/` changes; a stale copy carries authority it no longer has. Delete these three header lines before pasting into a chat model's instructions.

---

You write for RoomIQ: room-level market intelligence and underwriting for US rent-by-the-room (coliving) investors. RoomIQ has three modules: the Dashboard (markets, Market Score, seasonality, a submarket map), the Property Analyzer (property signal, room segments, rolling 7, 30, and 90-day windows, Evidence Quality, Visually Similar Rooms, Media Studio AI concepts), and the Property Predictor (underwrite any US address: baseline profile, forecast with formula, support level, and confidence; Deal Calculator on RoomIQ Pro; My Underwrites).

**Audiences. Pick one before writing. Never blend.**
- Acquiring investors (primary): "Know what each room can earn before you buy the house, and how much to trust the number."
- Operating hosts (secondary): "See how every room in your house earns against rooms like it."

**Positioning.** RoomIQ works in the unit this business runs on, the room, priced weekly. Short-term rental tools model nights and rent comps model whole units. Every RoomIQ forecast prints its formula, its comps, and a confidence label. Lead with visible evidence, never with accuracy.

**Words.** RoomIQ (one word). Property Predictor, Property Analyzer, Dashboard, Deal Calculator, My Underwrites, Media Studio, Visually Similar Rooms. "Forecast" is the output; "baseline profile" is the input form. "Estimated rental revenue", never income. "coliving", one word. "residents", not members or tenants. "Thin" means too little evidence, not weak demand.

**Status. Never write an unshipped capability as live.**
- Shipped (describe only as seen): market search (up to 3 cities, ZIPs, or a metro), seasonality, submarket map, supply map, property search, performance and revenue estimate, property signal, room segments, rolling windows, visual comps, AI upgrade concepts (watermarked), nearby coliving supply, revenue forecast for any US address, evidence lookback test.
- Partial (describe the visible part only): Market Score ranking, Evidence Quality, Deal Calculator (inputs only), My Underwrites.
- Unverified (name only, never describe output): market forecasts tab, flood overlay, filters, saved views, report export, property trends, room history, layout recommendation, amenity ROI, house rules, rent guidance, cohort outcomes, comp set review, garage conversion.
- Never mention: upgrade economics, market-move alerts, markets outside the US.

**Proof points, the closed set.** Customer proof: none. Write [PROOF POINT NEEDED]. Product facts you may state: the formula prints under every forecast; support level, confidence, comp count, and median comp distance are shown; scenarios are labeled "not a calibrated prediction interval"; revenue estimates say "Based on observed rents and occupancy, not collected payments."; AI concepts are watermarked "AI-GENERATED - NOT ACTUAL PROPERTY CONDITION". No coverage numbers.

**Do not say, say instead.**
- Accurate, precise, proven forecasts. Instead: every forecast shows its formula, comps, and confidence.
- Any market, complete coverage. Instead: underwrite any US address; where nearby evidence is thin, RoomIQ labels the forecast fallback support and shows its confidence.
- Any data source name, "scraped", "partnered with", "real-time". Instead: built from observed room listings in the markets RoomIQ covers; metrics show their as-of date.
- Income, earnings, guaranteed returns, best deals, lender-ready. Instead: model the deal with your own inputs, for information, not financial advice.
- AI-powered on everything. Instead: name the capability; only visual comps and AI concepts are AI.
- AI concepts as results or rent uplift. Instead: preview an AI concept of an upgrade, watermarked, with no validated economics yet.
- Prices, trials, limits, tier names other than RoomIQ Pro. Instead: nothing; pricing is undecided.
- Legal or compliant. Instead: compare a checklist with recorded local policies; not legal advice.
- House rules or resident criteria tied to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, disability, or source of income. Instead: conduct and property-use rules for every resident.
- "The only room-level tool", "better than AirDNA". Instead: "AirDNA is built for nightly stays. RoomIQ models weekly room rents and room occupancy."

**Channels.** In: founder-led demos and calls, education content, community answers (with disclosure), product-led trial, product and release copy. Out today: paid ads and cold outreach at volume. If asked, say it is out of scope for this go-to-market and offer a community post or a warm follow-up instead. Demos only in well-covered Sun Belt metros.

**How it is written.** Plain, numerate, candid, like an underwriting memo. Every number carries its unit and window (per room per week, per property per month). Say the uncomfortable part first. Short paragraphs, second person, one reader. No emoji. Banned words: leverage (finance sense too), unlock, seamless, robust, streamline, cutting-edge, empower, elevate, harness, supercharge, game-changing, best-in-class, crucial, vital. No em dashes.

**Before you return anything.** Check the draft against the status list, the proof points, and the do-not-say list. Fix what breaks. Then name, in one line, the rule the draft came closest to breaking.

**When you are unsure.** Write [NEEDS BRAIN] and keep going. Never fill a gap with an invention.

<<<END adapters/portable-control-layer.md>>>


<<<FILE adapters/mcp/README.md>>>

# MCP, the brain as tools any agent can call

`tools/mcp_server.py` serves this brain over the Model Context Protocol (stdio transport, newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0). Python 3.9+ standard library only: no install step, no network calls.

## What it exposes

| Kind | Name | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Tool | `brain_load_control_layer` | Router, writing rules, do-not-say, feature status, glossary, QA checklist. Call first. |
| Tool | `brain_load_for_task` | Files for one job: `demo`, `landing_page`, `content`, `competitive`, `product_copy`, `release_note`, `support`, `strategy`, `signal_intake`, `experiment`, and more |
| Tool | `brain_search` | BM25 over heading-level sections, rules ranked above examples |
| Tool | `brain_read` | One file by path |
| Tool | `brain_feature_status` | What may be claimed about a capability |
| Tool | `brain_glossary` | Canonical terms |
| Tool | `brain_decisions` | DECIDED, WORKING, OPEN decisions |
| Tool | `brain_lint` | Mechanical QA on a draft |
| Tool | `brain_metrics` | Innovation accounting rollup |
| Tool | `brain_log_signal`, `brain_log_activity` | Append-only intake. Disabled unless `--allow-write` |
| Resources | `brain:///<path>` | Every brain file |
| Prompts | one per job in `prompts/common-tasks.md` | Slash-command style prompts in clients that show them |

Writes are off by default so a read-only agent can never change the brain. Turn them on for the intake workflow you trust: `--allow-write` or `ROOMIQ_BRAIN_WRITE=1`. Writes only ever append entries to the two logs; every ledger change still goes through a pull request.

## Client configuration

Replace `/abs/path/to/RoomIQGTMBrain` with your checkout. In a product repo with the brain as a submodule, use `gtm-brain/tools/mcp_server.py`.

**Claude Code** (already registered in this repo by `.mcp.json`):
```bash
claude mcp add roomiq-gtm-brain -- python3 /abs/path/to/RoomIQGTMBrain/tools/mcp_server.py
```

**Claude Desktop**, `claude_desktop_config.json`:
```json
{ "mcpServers": { "roomiq-gtm-brain": { "command": "python3", "args": ["/abs/path/to/RoomIQGTMBrain/tools/mcp_server.py"] } } }
```

**Cursor**, `.cursor/mcp.json` (already in this repo):
```json
{ "mcpServers": { "roomiq-gtm-brain": { "command": "python3", "args": ["${workspaceFolder}/tools/mcp_server.py"] } } }
```

**VS Code with Copilot agent mode**, `.vscode/mcp.json` (already in this repo):
```json
{ "servers": { "roomiq-gtm-brain": { "type": "stdio", "command": "python3", "args": ["${workspaceFolder}/tools/mcp_server.py"] } } }
```

**Windsurf**, `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json`:
```json
{ "mcpServers": { "roomiq-gtm-brain": { "command": "python3", "args": ["/abs/path/to/RoomIQGTMBrain/tools/mcp_server.py"] } } }
```

**Codex CLI**, `~/.codex/config.toml`:
```toml
[mcp_servers.roomiq_gtm_brain]
command = "python3"
args = ["/abs/path/to/RoomIQGTMBrain/tools/mcp_server.py"]
```

**Gemini CLI**, `.gemini/settings.json` (already in this repo):
```json
{ "mcpServers": { "roomiq-gtm-brain": { "command": "python3", "args": ["tools/mcp_server.py"] } } }
```

**Zed**, `settings.json`:
```json
{ "context_servers": { "roomiq-gtm-brain": { "command": { "path": "python3", "args": ["/abs/path/to/RoomIQGTMBrain/tools/mcp_server.py"] } } } }
```

Client config formats change between versions. If a client rejects a snippet, check its current MCP documentation; the server side does not change.

## Smoke test without a client
```bash
printf '%s\n' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"smoke","version":"0"}}}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"brain_feature_status","arguments":{"query":"C27"}}}' \
  | python3 tools/mcp_server.py
```

## Agent pattern that works
1. `brain_load_control_layer` once per session.
2. `brain_load_for_task` for the job.
3. Draft.
4. `brain_lint` on the draft, fix errors, check warnings against the ledger.
5. Return the draft with the capability statuses used and the rule it came closest to breaking.

<<<END adapters/mcp/README.md>>>

<!-- roomiq-gtm-brain:begin -->
## RoomIQ go-to-market brain

The RoomIQ go-to-market lives in `gtm-brain/`. It is the source of truth for positioning, messaging, claims, product status, and voice. Do not restate strategy from memory when the brain settles it. This file is a generated pointer (`tools/brain.py adapters`); edit the brain, not this file.

Before any customer-facing writing (web pages, docs, release notes, UI strings, sales or support text, and LLM output shown to users), read in this order:

1. `gtm-brain/AGENTS.md`, the router.
2. `gtm-brain/rules/writing-rules.md`
3. `gtm-brain/rules/do-not-say.md`
4. `gtm-brain/rules/feature-status.md`
5. `gtm-brain/rules/glossary.md`

Pick one audience and never blend them: acquiring investors (primary) or operating hosts (secondary).

Non-negotiables:
- No forecast accuracy claims. Claim the visible evidence: formula, support level, confidence.
- "Any US address" always carries the fallback clause in the same sentence.
- Never name or imply the data source or a platform partnership.
- No prices, trials, limits, coverage numbers, or invented proof. Write `[PROOF POINT NEEDED]`.
- UNVERIFIED capabilities are named, never described. ROADMAP items are never mentioned.
- No em dashes and none of the banned words in the writing rules.

Run `python3 gtm-brain/tools/brain.py lint <file>` and `gtm-brain/ops/QA-checklist.md` before returning a draft. New market input goes to `gtm-brain/ops/signal-log.md` and work done to `gtm-brain/ops/activity-log.md`, never straight into copy.
<!-- roomiq-gtm-brain:end -->

<<<END adapters/consuming-repo/AGENTS.md>>>


<<<FILE tools/README.md>>>

# Tools, the brain as an executable system

Python 3.9+ standard library only. No install step, no network calls, no third-party packages. Markdown stays the source of truth; these tools read it, check it, export it, and append to its logs.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `brain_lib.py` | Shared parsers (ledgers, logs, decisions, experiments), linter, BM25 search, exports, adapter renderer |
| `brain.py` | The CLI. Run with `--help` |
| `mcp_server.py` | The brain over MCP (stdio JSON-RPC). See `adapters/mcp/README.md` |
| `templates/pointer-body.md.tmpl` | The single source for every tool adapter |
| `tests/test_brain.py` | Unit tests: parsers, linter, writers, adapters, MCP handshake |

## Common commands

```bash
python3 tools/brain.py audit                      # what CI runs
python3 tools/brain.py lint drafts/landing.md     # mechanical QA, exit 1 on errors
python3 tools/brain.py status unverified          # what may not be described
python3 tools/brain.py search "data source objection"
python3 tools/brain.py load demo --paths          # files a demo task loads
python3 tools/brain.py metrics                    # innovation accounting rollup
python3 tools/brain.py build                      # regenerate dist/
python3 tools/brain.py adapters --write           # regenerate tool adapters
python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/tests -v
```

Intake from the shell:

```bash
python3 tools/brain.py log-signal --type OBJECTION --source "demo, Dallas investor" \
  --verbatim "Where does your data come from?" --context "Stage 4, design partner"

python3 tools/brain.py log-activity --type DEMO --title "Design-partner session 1" \
  --what "Ran a Dallas townhouse through the Predictor" --audience A \
  --linked "EXP-001, A1, A2" --expected "Investor asks to run a second address within 7 days"
```

## Contracts other code can rely on
- `dist/ledgers.json`: features, claims, glossary, decisions, assumptions, experiments, signals, activities.
- `dist/brain.chunks.jsonl`: one JSON object per heading-level section, with `path`, `layer`, `always_load`, `heading`, `last_reviewed`, `brain_version`, `tokens_est`, `text`.
- `dist/brain.manifest.json`: every file with layer, purpose, size, token estimate, hash, and the load policy.
- `schemas/*.schema.json`: JSON Schema (2020-12) for signal, activity, experiment, assumption, decision, and feature objects. Webhook producers validate against these.

## Design rules for changes here
- Never write to `rules/` or `context/` from a tool. Ledger changes go through a reviewed pull request.
- Appends are the only writes, and they always carry the verbatim or the expected outcome.
- Output must be deterministic so `build --check` and `adapters --check` can gate CI.

<<<END tools/README.md>>>


<<<FILE .github/pull_request_template.md>>>

## What changed in the brain

<!-- One or two sentences. Name the signal, experiment, or founder answer that triggered it. -->

## Type
- [ ] PATCH (copy only: copy bank, templates, examples, reference wording)
- [ ] AMEND (a ledger in rules/, positioning, ICP, channels, or pricing)
- [ ] Intake (signal or activity entries only)
- [ ] Tooling (tools/, schemas/, adapters template, CI)

## AMEND checklist, in this order
- [ ] Ledger in `rules/` updated, `last_reviewed` bumped
- [ ] Master context section updated, `version`, `last_updated`, `status_notes` revised
- [ ] Dated entry in `ops/decisions.md`, including "What this does not change"
- [ ] Old phrasing searched and replaced in `ops/copy-bank.md`, templates, examples
- [ ] `adapters/portable-control-layer.md` regenerated and dated
- [ ] `python3 tools/brain.py build` and `python3 tools/brain.py adapters --write` run
- [ ] Affected live surfaces from `ops/asset-index.md` listed with owners

## Checks
- [ ] `python3 tools/brain.py audit` passes
- [ ] Any new customer-facing copy passed `python3 tools/brain.py lint` and `ops/QA-checklist.md`

<<<FILE sources/README.md>>>

# Sources, the evidence this brain distills

Load this when a ledger entry is questioned. The argument ends by opening the source.

Everything in `context/`, `rules/`, and `reference/` traces back to the artifacts below. When a source changes, update the master context and the affected ledger in `rules/` in the same change, then record it in `ops/decisions.md`.

## Source manifest

| # | Artifact | Type | What it settles | Dated | Location |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Screen inventory | Markdown, 15 screens | Verbatim UI copy, every visible number, observed vs inferred capability per screen | 2026-11-10 | `extracted/discovery/screen-inventory.md` |
| S2 | Working notes | Markdown, cross-screen analysis | IA map, glossary draft, data entities, monetization signals, third-party dependencies, 36 QA issues, 26 open questions | 2026-11-10 | `extracted/discovery/working-notes.md` |
| S3 | Feature classification | Markdown | The 32 features (C01 to C32) kept apart from 31 non-feature elements (E01 to E31), with evidence level per feature | 2026-11-10 | `extracted/discovery/feature-classification.md` |
| S4 | Coverage gaps | Markdown | 50 visible-but-unopened controls (A1 to A50) and 14 assumed SaaS screens (B1 to B14) still to capture | 2026-11-10 | `extracted/discovery/coverage-gaps.md` |
| S5 | Discovery README and intake log | Markdown | Batch dates, the facts-only PRD rule, synthesis status | 2026-11-10 | `extracted/discovery/README.md` |
| S6 | Product screenshots, batches 01 to 03 | 15 images (WEBP, PNG) | The primary evidence for S1 to S4 | 2026-11-10 | Kept out of this repo, see below |
| S7 | Competitive desk scan | Web search notes | Candidate competitor set and each rival's public positioning, unverified beyond public pages | 2026-11-13 | `reference/competitive-analysis.md` |
| S8 | GTM Brain skill | Method | The build procedure, file blueprint, compounding protocol | 2026-11-13 | `.claude/skills/go-to-market-brain/` |

## Why the screenshots are not in this repo

The screenshots show third-party listing photos, host display names, and the signed-in account's email address. Rights to show listing photos and host names are an open question (see `ops/decisions.md`, open item on data rights). The brain therefore records their location instead of copying them:

- Repository: `Saasrelaunchdev/roomIQGTMBuild`
- Path: `docs/discovery/screenshots/batch-01/` to `batch-03/`
- Commit at build time: `9ed7a8bfe272bd92b1bdc9e11b84e33e54ceb684`

## How the sources were read

1. Every extract in `extracted/discovery/` was read in full. Nothing was sampled.
2. Two evidence rules from the discovery pack carry into the brain unchanged:
   - **Facts only, traced to a screen.** A capability is described only as far as a screenshot shows it.
   - **Inferred is not observed.** Anything labeled `[Inferred]` or `[Q]` in the sources stays out of the shipped-capability list and becomes an open question or a working hypothesis.
3. Conflicts between sources: none found. The C1 to C62 capability list in `working-notes.md` is superseded by the C01 to C32 list in `feature-classification.md`, which the sources themselves state. The brain uses C01 to C32 everywhere.

## Source gaps (what no artifact settles yet)

Data provenance and rights, coverage numbers, pricing and tiers, the ICP the founder intends, channel mix, any customer proof, forecast accuracy (backtest), and the outputs of the 14 "button only" capabilities. Each is an open item in `ops/decisions.md` and a question in `ops/founder-gap-interview.md`.

<<<END sources/README.md>>>

# RoomIQ GTM Brain

> The governed go-to-market context repository for RoomIQ, room-level market intelligence and underwriting for US rent-by-the-room investors. Built from 15 product screenshots (2026-11-10) and a competitive desk scan (2026-11-13). This file indexes the repository for AI agents: read the routers, then the control layer, then only the task files you need. Never retrieve the control layer by search; load it whole.

## Routers (always loaded)
- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): router for Claude Code and Claude apps; wins if routers disagree.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): router for Codex, Cursor, Zed, Jules, opencode, Warp, and other AGENTS.md readers.
- [GEMINI.md](GEMINI.md): pointer for Gemini CLI.
- [README.md](README.md): human orientation, architecture, use cases, diagrams.

## Source of truth
- [Master GTM context](context/RoomIQ_GTM_Master_Context.md): the whole go-to-market in one read; Section 0 is written to the agent.

## Control layer (read before writing anything customer-facing)
- [Writing rules](rules/writing-rules.md): mechanics, banned words, tone, channel discipline, signature lines.
- [Do not say](rules/do-not-say.md): forbidden claims with safe replacements, fair housing, demo rules, scoped superlatives.
- [Feature status](rules/feature-status.md): SHIPPED, PARTIAL, UNVERIFIED, IN BUILD, ROADMAP for C01 to C32 and R01 to R03; known defects.
- [Glossary](rules/glossary.md): canonical product, metric, and category vocabulary.
- [QA checklist](ops/QA-checklist.md): the pre-ship gate.

## Reference (load on demand)
- [Product surface](reference/product-surface.md): RoomIQ as built, IA, workflow, entities, reconciling numbers.
- [Feature matrix](reference/feature-matrix.md): which capability leads, hooks, is table stakes, or is held.
- [ICP and personas](reference/icp-personas.md): acquiring investors, operating hosts, buying committee, design partners.
- [Positioning](reference/positioning.md): category, statement, reframes, one-liners.
- [Value proposition, investors](reference/value-proposition-investors.md): Audience A pillars and reasons to believe.
- [Value proposition, operators](reference/value-proposition-operators.md): Audience B pillars and reasons to believe.
- [Customer journey funnels](reference/customer-journey.md): two funnels, stage by stage, activation definition.
- [Competitive market analysis](reference/competitive-analysis.md): market shape, vectors, wedge, dated public facts.
- [Competitor battlecards](reference/competitor-battlecards.md): strength, gap, how RoomIQ wins, per rival.
- [Objection handling](reference/objection-handling.md): data source, accuracy, coverage, AI images, pricing, legal.
- [Marketing campaigns](reference/marketing-campaigns.md): five campaigns, the assumption each tests, asset backlog.
- [Content engine](reference/content-engine.md): channel engine for education content and communities.
- [Demo playbook](reference/demo-playbook.md): channel engine for founder-led demos, landmines, screenshot rules.
- [Trust and risk](reference/trust-and-risk.md): data rights, AI derivatives, financial outputs, fair housing, disclosures.
- [Pricing and packaging](reference/pricing-packaging.md): monetization signals as hypotheses; pricing is OPEN.
- [Metrics methodology](reference/metrics-methodology.md): how each number is built, verified versus working.
- [Innovation accounting](reference/innovation-accounting.md): baseline, tune, pivot or persevere; the snowball data flow.

## Innovation accounting (state that compounds)
- [Assumptions](innovation/assumptions.md): leap-of-faith assumptions with riskiness and status.
- [Experiments](innovation/experiments.md): pre-registered experiments with thresholds set before results.
- [Metrics](innovation/metrics.md): North Star, input metrics, vanity guards, learning velocity.

## Operations and state
- [Decision log](ops/decisions.md): DECIDED, WORKING, OPEN, with rationale and what each does not change.
- [Signal log](ops/signal-log.md): raw market input, verbatim, with disposition.
- [Activity log](ops/activity-log.md): what the team did, expected outcome written first.
- [Copy bank](ops/copy-bank.md): checked language and the closed proof set.
- [Asset index](ops/asset-index.md): sources, live surfaces, adapters, generated artifacts.
- [Review cadence](ops/review-cadence.md): rituals, owners, staleness, authority.
- [Founder gap interview](ops/founder-gap-interview.md): 21 questions with the defaults the brain runs on.
- [Baseline snapshot](snapshots/2026-11-13-baseline.md): day-zero capture.

## Templates
- [Template library](templates/README.md): one per channel in the working mix, none for excluded channels.
- [Landing page](templates/landing-page.md), [One-pager](templates/one-pager.md), [Demo script](templates/demo-script.md), [Education article](templates/seo-article.md), [Social post](templates/social-post.md), [Community answer](templates/community-answer.md), [Warm outreach](templates/outreach-warm.md), [Release note](templates/release-note.md), [In-app copy](templates/in-app-copy.md)

## Prompts and finished assets

## Portability (doors for other tools)

- Skill pointers written by the installer: [Cursor skill rule](.cursor/rules/go-to-market-brain.mdc), [Windsurf skill rule](.windsurf/rules/go-to-market-brain.md)
- [Consuming-repo adapters](adapters/consuming-repo/AGENTS.md): pre-rendered for a product repo with the brain at `gtm-brain/`.

## Machine-readable exports (generated, do not edit)
- [Single-file bundle](dist/roomiq-gtm-brain.bundle.md): control layer plus master context, guardrails last.
- [Full text](dist/llms-full.txt): every brain file concatenated.
- [Manifest](dist/brain.manifest.json): files, layers, purposes, sizes, hashes, load policy.
- [Chunks](dist/brain.chunks.jsonl): heading-level chunks with metadata for vector stores.
- [Ledgers](dist/ledgers.json): every ledger and log as JSON.

## Tooling
- [Tools guide](tools/README.md): CLI, MCP server, tests, contracts.
- [Brain change PR template](.github/pull_request_template.md): the AMEND order as a checklist.
- [Sources manifest](sources/README.md): what each source settles; why screenshots are kept out.

<<<FILE templates/community-answer.md>>>

# Template, community answer

Audience: [A / B]. Where: [forum thread / group post / podcast Q&A]. The question, verbatim: "[paste]"

## Structure
1. **Answer the question first**, fully, without RoomIQ. Most of the value lives here.
2. **Show the reasoning** with one worked number, unit and window stated.
3. **Name the limit** of the answer: what you would need to know about their house.
4. **Mention RoomIQ only if it directly helps**, in one sentence, disclosed as your own product: "Disclosure: I'm building RoomIQ, which does X."
5. **No link unless the community allows it.**

## Rules
- Disclosure is mandatory whenever RoomIQ is mentioned.
- Never answer legal questions beyond "check local occupancy and rooming-house rules".
- Never suggest house rules tied to a protected class.
- Log the question as a LANGUAGE signal in `ops/signal-log.md`, verbatim.

## Guardrails
`rules/writing-rules.md` and `rules/do-not-say.md`. Lint and QA before posting.

<<<END templates/community-answer.md>>>


<<<FILE templates/demo-script.md>>>

# Template, demo script

Audience: [A investors / B operators]. Length: [20 min live / 2 min recorded]. Covered metro: [name]. Address tested today: [yes / no, stop if no].
Method: `reference/demo-playbook.md`. Voice: `examples/demo-talk-track.md`.

## Before
- [ ] Address in a covered metro, forecast run today, confidence better than Low.
- [ ] Room Mix filled for every bedroom (avoids D-Q26).
- [ ] Deal Calculator inputs typed, including interest rate (avoids D-Q30).
- [ ] Host names and photos blurred if recorded for public use.

## Beats
1. **Open (30 seconds).** Their question, in their words. "You've got a house under contract and a room rent number in a spreadsheet."
2. **Market (2 minutes).** Dashboard, preset metro, Market Score list, map bands. Say what Thin means.
3. **Comparable property (4 minutes).** Analyzer: signal, room segments, best spread, windows. Do one reconciliation out loud.
4. **Their address (6 minutes).** Predictor: supply, baseline profile, run, read the formula, support, and confidence aloud.
5. **The deal (4 minutes).** Deal Calculator with typed inputs. "For information, not financial advice."
6. **Close (1 minute).** One call to action.

## Spoken rules
Short sentences. Read on-screen labels before interpreting them. Never skip a confidence or fallback label for pacing. Nothing UNVERIFIED shown as usable.

## After
Log the activity and every signal within 24 hours (`ops/activity-log.md`, `ops/signal-log.md`).

## Guardrails
`rules/writing-rules.md` writing for the ear. `rules/feature-status.md` demo rule. Lint and QA the script before recording.

<<<END templates/demo-script.md>>>


<<<FILE templates/in-app-copy.md>>>

# Template, in-app copy

For engineers and designers editing UI strings, empty states, errors, tooltips, banners, and paywall prompts in the RoomIQ product. Also the guardrail spec for any LLM-generated text shown inside the product.

## String review fields
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Location | Module, step, component |
| Current string | verbatim |
| Proposed string | verbatim |
| Glossary terms used | from `rules/glossary.md` |
| Ledger check | capability IDs and status |
| Reason | defect ID or rule |

## Rules for product strings
- Use glossary terms exactly: Forecast for the output, baseline profile for the inputs.
- Plurals: "1 result", "2 results"; "1 room", "2 rooms".
- Subject-verb agreement in generated sentences: "Only 1 of 3 bedrooms has".
- Every banner that explains a number must agree with the number on the same screen.
- Empty states say what to do next in one sentence.
- Tooltips define, never sell. Pull definitions from `reference/metrics-methodology.md`, verified rows first.
- Paywall prompts say what Pro adds, never prices until D-11 closes.

## Rules for LLM-generated text inside the product
- House-rule recommendations: never reference a protected class. Conduct and property use only.
- Recommendations never promise rent, occupancy, or returns.
- Every generated recommendation carries its evidence basis or says it has none.
- Run outputs through `python3 tools/brain.py lint` in tests; treat any hit on a hard ban as a failing test.

## Guardrails
`rules/glossary.md`, `rules/do-not-say.md`, `rules/feature-status.md`. Matching example: `examples/in-app-copy-fixes.md`.

<<<END templates/in-app-copy.md>>>


<<<FILE templates/landing-page.md>>>

# Template, landing page

Audience: [A investors / B operators]. Pick one. Never blend.
Funnel stage: [3 solution aware / 4 evaluating]
Voice reference: `examples/landing-hero-investors.md`

1. **Hero.** One promise in the audience's words, from `ops/copy-bank.md`. Subhead names what RoomIQ is and who it is for. One primary call to action.
2. **The problem as they feel it.** Investors: room rents typed into a spreadsheet. Operators: a room that keeps sitting empty. No product yet.
3. **The reframe.** One line from the copy bank reframes section.
4. **What it is.** One paragraph. Room-level, weekly rents, US rent-by-the-room.
5. **Pillar 1.** Headline, then reasons to believe from the audience's value proposition file. SHIPPED capabilities only.
6. **Pillar 2.** Same shape.
7. **Pillar 3.** Same shape. PARTIAL capabilities: describe the visible part only.
8. **How it works.** Three or four steps that match the real flow (Dashboard, Analyzer, Predictor).
9. **Show the evidence.** One screenshot from a covered metro, host names and photos blurred, formula and confidence label visible.
10. **Objections.** The two from `reference/objection-handling.md` that this stage raises, usually data source and accuracy.
11. **Proof.** `[PROOF POINT NEEDED]` until the closed set holds customer proof.
12. **Comparison.** Honest, using `reference/competitor-battlecards.md`, rival strength first.
13. **FAQ.** Real questions, including "not yet" answers. No prices.
14. **Close.** Same call to action as the hero.

## Guardrails
One audience. Every capability checked in `rules/feature-status.md`. "Any US address" carries the fallback clause. No accuracy, coverage, data-source, or price claims (`rules/do-not-say.md`). Run `python3 tools/brain.py lint` and `ops/QA-checklist.md` before shipping.

<<<END templates/landing-page.md>>>

# Template, one-pager

Audience: [A investors / B operators]. Purpose: [design-partner leave-behind / lender briefing by the investor / community partner brief].

## Structure
- **Header.** What RoomIQ is, in one line from `ops/copy-bank.md`.
- **The problem.** Two sentences, in the audience's language.
- **Three pillars.** One line each, from that audience's value proposition file.
- **How the numbers are built.** Three bullets from `reference/metrics-methodology.md`, verified rows only.
- **What is live today.** SHIPPED capabilities, plainly. PARTIAL ones with their visible part. Nothing else.
- **Proof.** Product facts from the closed set. Customer proof: `[PROOF POINT NEEDED]`.
- **Next step.** One call to action.
- **Footer.** "Estimates are based on observed rents and occupancy, not collected payments. For information, not financial advice."

## Guardrails
Fits one page. One audience. No accuracy, coverage, or price claims. No data-source names. Lint and QA before sending.

<<<FILE templates/outreach-warm.md>>>

# Template, warm outreach

For people who asked, engaged, or were introduced. Not for cold lists: outreach at volume is out of scope (D-10).
Audience: [A / B]. Relationship: [asked in a thread / introduced by / met at]. Purpose: [design-partner invite / follow-up after a demo].

## Structure
- **Subject or first line.** Their context, not ours: "Your question about the garage conversion in [city]".
- **Why you are writing.** One sentence tied to what they said or did.
- **The offer.** One concrete thing: "I can run that address through RoomIQ with you in 30 minutes and show you the room-level forecast, including how confident it is."
- **The honest limit.** "If the address is in a market with thin evidence, it will say so."
- **One ask.** A time, or a yes or no.

## Rules
Under 120 words. No attachments on first contact. No prices. No claims beyond the copy bank. Log the outreach as an activity and the reply, verbatim, as a signal.

## Guardrails
`rules/writing-rules.md` and `rules/do-not-say.md`. Lint and QA before sending.

<<<END templates/outreach-warm.md>>>


<<<FILE templates/release-note.md>>>

# Template, release note

Audience: existing users (A and B may share a changelog; individual notes target one). Capability IDs touched: [C..]. Status change: [from X to Y].

## Order of operations (before writing a word)
1. Update `rules/feature-status.md` for every capability this release touches.
2. If a defect in "Known defects that gate claims" is fixed, remove it there and in `reference/demo-playbook.md`.
3. Then write the note.

## Structure
- **Title.** What changed, in the product's own labels.
- **What you can do now.** One to three sentences, present tense, SHIPPED only.
- **Why it matters.** One sentence tied to a job in `reference/icp-personas.md`.
- **Where to find it.** Module and step, exactly as labeled in the UI.
- **Limits.** Anything partial, said plainly.

## Rules
No "coming soon" lists in a release note. No accuracy claims for model changes; describe what changed in the method or the labels. Glossary terms exactly.

## Guardrails
Ledger before copy, always. Lint and QA before publishing. Log the release as an activity (type RELEASE).

<<<END templates/release-note.md>>>


<<<FILE templates/seo-article.md>>>

# Template, education article

Audience: [A / B]. Stage: [2 problem aware / 3 solution aware]. Archetype: [worked example / method piece / myth check / honest limitation / operator teardown]. Search question: [the phrase the reader types].
Method: `reference/content-engine.md`.

## Plan (write before drafting)
- Takeaway in one sentence:
- The one question this answers:
- Capability IDs mentioned and their status:
- The single call to action:

## Structure
1. **Title.** The search question or its answer. Under 65 characters.
2. **Opening.** The reader's situation in two sentences. No product.
3. **The method.** How to think about the variable, with a worked example and every unit stated.
4. **Where it goes wrong.** The common mistake, stated plainly.
5. **Doing it with evidence.** One section showing how RoomIQ handles it, SHIPPED capabilities only, one blurred screenshot.
6. **The limit.** What evidence cannot tell you here.
7. **Call to action.** One.

## Guardrails
Teach before showing. Every number carries unit and window. No market statistics published as data (G11, G12). No accuracy, coverage, or price claims. Lint and QA before publishing.

<<<END templates/seo-article.md>>>


<<<FILE templates/social-post.md>>>

# Template, social post

Audience: [A / B]. Platform: [LinkedIn / X / community group]. Archetype: [worked example / method / myth check / honest limitation].

## Structure
- **Line 1, the hook.** A number with its unit, a decision, or a candid limit (patterns in `reference/content-engine.md`).
- **Lines 2 to 5, the substance.** One idea. Show the arithmetic if there is any.
- **Line 6, the takeaway.** What the reader should do differently.
- **Optional last line.** One call to action, or none. Communities often reward none.

## Rules
- One idea per post.
- No hashtags stacked; one at most where the platform expects it.
- No emoji.
- Screenshots blurred: host names, listing photos, account details.

## Guardrails
`rules/writing-rules.md` and `rules/do-not-say.md`. No accuracy, coverage, or price claims. Lint and QA before posting.

<<<END templates/social-post.md>>>
